piezometer.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring high pressures

pipet.definition: measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube used to measure or transfer precise volumes of a liquid by drawing the liquid up into the tube

dropper.definition: pipet consisting of a small tube with a vacuum bulb at one end for drawing liquid in and releasing it a drop at a time

pitot-static_tube.definition: measuring instrument consisting of a combined Pitot tube and static tube that measures total and static pressure; used in aircraft to measure airspeed

pitot_tube.definition: measuring instrument consisting of a right-angled tube with an open end that is directed in opposition to the flow of a fluid and used to measure the velocity of fluid flow

plethysmograph.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring changes in volume of a part or organ or whole body (usually resulting from fluctuations in the amount of blood it contains)

body_plethysmograph.definition: plethysmograph consisting of a chamber surrounding the entire body; used in studies of respiration

digital_plethysmograph.definition: plethysmograph applied to a digit of the hand or foot to measure skin blood flow

potentiometer (measuring_instrument).definition: a measuring instrument for measuring direct current electromotive forces

quadrant (measuring_instrument).definition: a measuring instrument for measuring altitude of heavenly bodies

radar.definition: measuring instrument in which the echo of a pulse of microwave radiation is used to detect and locate distant objects

doppler_radar.definition: radar that uses the Doppler shift to measure velocity

early_warning_radar.definition: a radar that is part of an early warning system

three-dimensional_radar.definition: radar that will report altitude as well as azimuth and distance of a target

weather_radar.definition: radar that is able to detect clouds and precipitation

rangefinder.definition: a measuring instrument (acoustic or optical or electronic) for finding the distance of an object

refractometer.definition: measuring instrument for measuring the refractive index of a substance

rheometer.definition: an instrument for measuring the flow of liquids (especially arterial blood)

scale (measuring_instrument).definition: a measuring instrument for weighing; shows amount of mass

balance (scale).definition: a scale for weighing; depends on pull of gravity

beam_balance.definition: a balance consisting of a lever with two equal arms and a pan suspended from each arm

analytical_balance.definition: a beam balance of great precision used in quantitative chemical analysis

electronic_balance.definition: a balance that generates a current proportional to the displacement of the pan

microbalance.definition: balance for weighing very small objects

spring_balance.definition: a balance that measure weight by the tension on a helical spring

steelyard.definition: a portable balance consisting of a pivoted bar with arms of unequal length

weighbridge.definition: platform scale flush with a roadway for weighing vehicles and cattle etc

sclerometer.definition: a measuring instrument that measures the hardness of materials by penetrating them with a stylus that has a diamond point

sector (measuring_instrument).definition: measuring instrument consisting of two graduated arms hinged at one end

seismograph.definition: a measuring instrument for detecting and measuring the intensity and direction and duration of movements of the ground (as an earthquake)

sextant.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring the angular distance between celestial objects; resembles an octant

spherometer.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring the curvature of a surface

spirograph.definition: a measuring instrument for recording the depth and rapidity of breathing movements

spirometer.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring the vital capacity of the lungs

static_tube.definition: a measuring instrument used to measure static pressure in a stream of fluid

synchroscope.definition: an instrument that indicates whether two periodic motions are synchronous (especially an instrument that enables a pilot to synchronize the propellers of a plane that has two or more engines)

tachometer.definition: measuring instrument for indicating speed of rotation

tachograph.definition: a tachometer that produces a graphical record of its readings; used to record the speed and duration of trips in a motor vehicle

tape (measuring_instrument).definition: measuring instrument consisting of a narrow strip (cloth or metal) marked in inches or centimeters and used for measuring lengths

alcohol_thermometer.definition: thermometer consisting of a glass capillary tube marked with degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit and containing alcohol which rises or falls as it expands or contracts with changes in temperature

candy_thermometer.definition: a thermometer used to determine the temperature of candy syrups during cooking

centigrade_thermometer.definition: a thermometer calibrated in degrees centigrade

cryometer.definition: a thermometer designed to measure low temperatures

dry-bulb_thermometer.definition: an ordinary thermometer with a dry bulb; used to measure the air temperature

fahrenheit_thermometer.definition: a thermometer calibrated in degrees Fahrenheit

gas_thermometer.definition: thermometer that measures temperature by changes in the pressure of a gas kept at constant volume

maximum_and_minimum_thermometer.definition: thermometer that records the highest and lowest temperatures reached during a period of time

meat_thermometer.definition: a thermometer that is inserted into the center of a roast (with the top away from the heat source); used to measure how well done the meat is

mercury_thermometer.definition: thermometer consisting of mercury contained in a bulb at the bottom of a graduated sealed glass capillary tube marked in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit; mercury expands with a rise in temperature causing a thin thread of mercury to rise in the tube

beckman_thermometer.definition: a mercury thermometer that measures small differences or changes in temperature

clinical_thermometer.definition: a mercury thermometer designed to measure the temperature of the human body; graduated to cover a range a few degrees on either side of the normal body temperature

oven_thermometer.definition: a thermometer that registers the temperature inside an oven

pyrometer.definition: a thermometer designed to measure high temperatures

optical_pyrometer.definition: a pyrometer that uses the color of the light emitted by a hot object

pyrometric_cone.definition: a pyrometer consisting of a series of cones that melt at different temperatures

radiation_pyrometer.definition: a pyrometer for estimating the temperature of distant sources of heat; radiation is focussed on a thermojunction connected in circuit with a galvanometer

resistance_pyrometer.definition: pyrometer that measures high temperatures by the resistance in a heated wire

reaumur_thermometer.definition: an alcohol thermometer calibrated in degrees Reaumur

resistance_thermometer.definition: thermometer that measures temperature by changes in the resistance of a spiral of platinum wire

reversing_thermometer.definition: a thermometer that registers the temperature in deep waters

self-registering_thermometer.definition: a thermometer that records the temperature automatically

telethermometer.definition: a thermometer that registers the temperature at some distant point

thermocouple.definition: a kind of thermometer consisting of two wires of different metals that are joined at both ends; one junction is at the temperature to be measured and the other is held at a fixed lower temperature; the current generated in the circuit is proportional to the temperature difference

thermoelectric_thermometer.definition: a thermometer that uses thermoelectric current to measure temperature

thermograph (thermometer).definition: a thermometer that records temperature variations on a graph as a function of time

thermopile.definition: a kind of thermometer for measuring heat radiation; consists of several thermocouple junctions in series

wet-bulb_thermometer.definition: a thermometer with a bulb that is covered with moist muslin; used in a psychrometer to measure humidity

timepiece.definition: a measuring instrument or device for keeping time

atomic_clock.definition: a timepiece that derives its time scale from the vibration of atoms or molecules

ammonia_clock.definition: an atomic clock based on vibrational frequency of the nitrogen atom in the ammonia molecule

caesium_clock.definition: an atomic clock based on the energy difference between two states of the caesium nucleus in a magnetic field

clock.definition: a timepiece that shows the time of day

alarm_clock.definition: a clock that wakes a sleeper at some preset time

analog_clock.definition: a clock that displays the time of day by the position of hands on a dial

chronometer.definition: an accurate clock (especially used in navigation)

cuckoo_clock.definition: clock that announces the hours with a sound like the call of the cuckoo

digital_clock.definition: a clock that displays the time of day digitally

electric_clock.definition: a clock using a small electric motor

pendulum_clock.definition: a clock regulated by a pendulum

grandfather_clock.definition: a pendulum clock enclosed in a tall narrow case

system_clock (clock).definition: a time-of-day clock in a computer system

time_clock.definition: clock used to record the hours that people work

turret_clock.definition: a clock with more than one dial to show the time in all directions from a tower

wall_clock.definition: a clock mounted on a wall

water_clock.definition: clock that measures time by the escape of water

sandglass.definition: timepiece in which the passage of time is indicated by the flow of sand from one transparent container to another through a narrow passage

egg_timer.definition: a sandglass that runs for three minutes; used to time the boiling of eggs

hourglass.definition: a sandglass that runs for sixty minutes

sundial.definition: timepiece that indicates the daylight hours by the shadow that the gnomon casts on a calibrated dial

timer (timepiece).definition: a timepiece that measures a time interval and signals its end

chronograph.definition: an accurate timer for recording time

parking_meter.definition: a coin-operated timer located next to a parking space; depositing money into it entitles you to park your car there for a specified length of time

stopwatch.definition: a timepiece that can be started or stopped for exact timing (as of a race)

analog_watch.definition: a watch that represents time by the position of hands on a dial

digital_watch.definition: a watch with a digital display

hunter (watch).definition: a watch with a hinged metal lid to protect the crystal

pendulum_watch.definition: (18th century) a watch with a balance wheel having a fake pendulum attached to it

pocket_watch.definition: a watch that is carried in a small watch pocket

stem-winder.definition: a watch that is wound by turning a knob at the stem

wristwatch.definition: a watch that is worn strapped to the wrist

tonometer.definition: measuring instrument for measuring tension or pressure (especially for measuring intraocular pressure in testing for glaucoma)

torsion_balance.definition: measuring instrument designed to measure small forces by the torsion they exert on a thin wire

variometer.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring variations in a magnetic field

venturi_tube.definition: a short tube inserted into a pipeline and used to measure the quantity of a liquid that is flowing in the pipeline

viscometer.definition: a measuring instrument for measuring viscosity

wattmeter.definition: an instrument for measuring in watts the flow of power in an electrical circuit

medical_instrument.definition: instrument used in the practice of medicine

ballistocardiograph.definition: a medical instrument that measures the mechanical force of cardiac contractions and the amount of blood passing through the heart during a specified period by measuring the recoil of the body as blood is pumped from the ventricles

bronchoscope.definition: a slender tubular instrument used to examine the bronchial tubes

cardiograph.definition: medical instrument that records electric currents associated with contractions of the heart

dialyzer.definition: a medical instrument for separating substances in solution by unequal diffusion through semipermeable membranes

artificial_kidney.definition: a machine that uses dialysis to remove impurities and waste products from the bloodstream before returning the blood to the patient's body

diathermy_machine.definition: a medical instrument for local heating of bodily tissues for medical purposes

microwave_diathermy_machine.definition: diathermy machine that uses microwave radiation as the source of heat

shortwave_diathermy_machine.definition: a diathermy machine that uses short wave radiation as the source of heat

electroencephalograph.definition: medical instrument that records electric currents generated by the brain

electromyograph.definition: a medical instrument that records the electrical waves associated with the activity of skeletal muscles

endoscope.definition: a long slender medical instrument for examining the interior of a bodily organ or performing minor surgery

arthroscope.definition: a type of endoscope that is inserted into a joint for visual examination

colonoscope.definition: an elongated fiberoptic endoscope for examining the entire colon from cecum to rectum

culdoscope.definition: a specialized endoscope for visually examining a woman's pelvic organs

gastroscope.definition: a type of endoscope for visually examining the stomach

laparoscope.definition: a slender endoscope inserted through an incision in the abdominal wall in order to examine the abdominal organs or to perform minor surgery

proctoscope.definition: an endoscope for examining the rectum

sigmoidoscope.definition: an endoscope (a flexible fiberoptic probe) for examining the sigmoid colon

fiberscope.definition: a flexible medical instrument involving fiber optics that is used to examine internal organs

keratoscope.definition: medical instrument to examine the cornea in order to detect irregularities in its anterior surface

laryngoscope.definition: a medical instrument for examining the larynx

ophthalmoscope.definition: medical instrument for examining the retina of the eye

orthoscope.definition: an ophthalmoscope with a layer of water to neutralize the refraction of the cornea

otoscope.definition: medical instrument consisting of a magnifying lens and light; used for examining the external ear (the auditory meatus and especially the tympanic membrane)

polygraph.definition: a medical instrument that records several physiological processes simultaneously (e.g., pulse rate and blood pressure and respiration and perspiration)

lie_detector.definition: a polygraph that records bodily changes sometimes associated with lying

rhinoscope.definition: medical instrument consisting of a mirror mounted at an angle on a rod; used to examine the nasal passages (through the nasopharynx)

speculum (medical_instrument).definition: a medical instrument for dilating a bodily passage or cavity in order to examine the interior

stethoscope.definition: a medical instrument for listening to the sounds generated inside the body

fetoscope.definition: a stethoscope placed on the pregnant woman's abdomen to listen for the fetal heartbeat

surgical_instrument.definition: a medical instrument used in surgery

curette.definition: a surgical instrument shaped like a scoop to remove tissue from a bodily cavity

dermatome.definition: a surgical instrument used to cut very thin slices of skin

dilator.definition: a surgical instrument that is used to dilate or distend an opening or an organ

hemostat.definition: a surgical instrument that stops bleeding by clamping the blood vessel

photocoagulator.definition: surgical instrument containing a laser for use in photocoagulation

probe.definition: a flexible slender surgical instrument with a blunt end that is used to explore wounds or body cavities

retractor.definition: surgical instrument that holds back the edges of a surgical incision

snare (surgical_instrument).definition: a surgical instrument consisting of wire hoop that can be drawn tight around the base of polyps or small tumors to sever them; used especially in body cavities

trepan (surgical_instrument).definition: a surgical instrument used to remove sections of bone from the skull

syringe.definition: a medical instrument used to inject or withdraw fluids

douche.definition: a small syringe with detachable nozzles; used for vaginal lavage and enemas

hypodermic_syringe.definition: a piston syringe that is fitted with a hypodermic needle for giving injections

autoinjector.definition: a hypodermic syringe to use in injecting yourself with a liquid

thermograph (medical_instrument).definition: medical instrument that uses an infrared camera to reveal temperature variations on the surface of the body

sonar.definition: a measuring instrument that sends out an acoustic pulse in water and measures distances in terms of the time for the echo of the pulse to return

artificial_horizon.definition: a navigational instrument based on a gyroscope; it artificially provides a simulated horizon for the pilot

gyrocompass.definition: a compass that does not depend on magnetism but uses a gyroscope instead

magnetic_compass.definition: compass based on an indicator (as a magnetic needle) that points to the magnetic north

compass_card.definition: compass in the form of a card that rotates so that 0 degrees or North points to magnetic north

depth_finder.definition: navigational instrument used to measure the depth of a body of water (as by ultrasound or radar)

sonic_depth_finder.definition: depth finder for determining depth of water or a submerged object by means of ultrasound waves

inclinometer (navigational_instrument).definition: an instrument showing the angle that an aircraft makes with the horizon

optical_instrument.definition: an instrument designed to aid vision

binoculars.definition: an optical instrument designed for simultaneous use by both eyes

esophagoscope.definition: an optical instrument for examining the inside of the esophagus

jeweler's_glass.definition: an optical instrument used by jewelers; has one or more lenses and is used to view features not readily seen

periscope.definition: an optical instrument that provides a view of an otherwise obstructed field

projector (optical_instrument).definition: an optical instrument that projects an enlarged image onto a screen

epidiascope.definition: an optical projector that gives images of both transparent and opaque objects

movie_projector.definition: projects successive frames from a reel of film to create moving pictures

bioscope (movie_projector).definition: a kind of early movie projector

overhead_projector.definition: a projector operated by a speaker; projects the image over the speaker's head

slide_projector.definition: projector that projects an enlarged image of a slide onto a screen

magic_lantern.definition: an early form of slide projector

sights.definition: an optical instrument for aiding the eye in aiming, as on a firearm or surveying instrument

bombsight.definition: a sighting device in an aircraft for aiming bombs

gunsight.definition: a sight used for aiming a gun

battle_sight.definition: an arrangement of sights that makes possible the rapid aiming of a firearm at short ranges

open_sight.definition: rear gunsight having an open notch instead of a peephole or telescope

panoramic_sight.definition: gunsight (a telescopic device for an artillery piece) that can be rotated horizontally in a full circle

peep_sight.definition: rear gunsight having an adjustable eyepiece with a small aperture through which the front sight and the target are aligned

sight_setting.definition: the adjustment of a gunsight for elevation and windage on a particular range under favorable light conditions

zero.definition: the sight setting that will cause a projectile to hit the center of the target with no wind blowing

telescopic_sight.definition: gunsight consisting of a telescope on a firearm for use as a sight

spectacles.definition: optical instrument consisting of a frame that holds a pair of lenses for correcting defective vision

bifocals.definition: eyeglasses having two focal lengths, one for near vision and the other for far vision

goggles.definition: tight-fitting spectacles worn to protect the eyes

lorgnette.definition: eyeglasses that are held to the eyes with a long handle

pince-nez.definition: spectacles clipped to the nose by a spring

sunglasses.definition: spectacles that are darkened or polarized to protect the eyes from the glare of the sun

spectroscope.definition: an optical instrument for spectrographic analysis

mass_spectrometer.definition: spectroscope for obtaining a mass spectrum by deflecting ions into a thin slit and measuring the ion current with an electrometer

mass_spectrograph.definition: a mass spectrometer that produces a graphical representation of the mass spectrum

spectrograph.definition: a spectroscope by which spectra can be photographed

plotter (instrument).definition: an instrument (usually driven by a computer) for drawing graphs or pictures

accelerator (scientific_instrument).definition: a scientific instrument that increases the kinetic energy of charged particles

betatron.definition: accelerates a continuous beam of electrons to high speeds by means of the electric field produced by changing magnetic flux

charge-exchange_accelerator.definition: an accelerator in which high-energy ions escape from plasma following charge exchange

cockcroft_and_walton_accelerator.definition: a high-voltage machine in which rectifiers charge capacitors that discharge and drive charged particles through an accelerating tube

collider.definition: an accelerator in which two beams of particles are forced to collide head on

electron_accelerator.definition: collider that consists of an accelerator that collides electrons and positrons

proton_accelerator.definition: a collider that collides beams of protons and antiprotons

superconducting_supercollider.definition: a collider that operates at very low temperatures

cyclotron.definition: an accelerator that imparts energies of several million electron-volts to rapidly moving particles

bevatron.definition: a cyclotron that accelerates protons up to several billion electron volts

synchrocyclotron.definition: cyclotron that achieves relativistic velocities by modulating the frequency of the accelerating electric field

synchrotron.definition: cyclotron in which the electric field is maintained at a constant frequency

cosmotron.definition: a large proton synchrotron; uses frequency modulation of an electric field to accelerate protons

linear_accelerator.definition: ions are accelerated along a linear path by voltage differences on electrodes along the path

console (scientific_instrument).definition: a scientific instrument consisting of displays and an input device that an operator can use to monitor and control a system (especially a computer system)

hodoscope.definition: (physics) scientific instrument that traces the path of a charged particle

kicksorter.definition: scientific instrument consisting of an electronic circuit that permits only voltage pulses of predetermined height to pass

kymograph.definition: scientific instrument consisting of a rotating drum holding paper on which a stylus traces a continuous record (as of breathing or blood pressure)

magnetograph.definition: a scientific instrument that registers magnetic variations (especially variations of the earth's magnetic field)

magnifier.definition: a scientific instrument that magnifies an image

microscope.definition: magnifier of the image of small objects

angioscope.definition: a modified microscope used to study capillary vessels

electron_microscope.definition: a microscope that is similar in purpose to a light microscope but achieves much greater resolving power by using a parallel beam of electrons to illuminate the object instead of a beam of light

field-emission_microscope.definition: electron microscope used to observe the surface structure of a solid

light_microscope.definition: microscope consisting of an optical instrument that magnifies the image of an object

binocular_microscope.definition: a light microscope adapted to the use of both eyes

operating_microscope.definition: binocular microscope used in surgery to provide a clear view of small and inaccessible parts of the body (as in microsurgery)

compound_microscope.definition: light microscope that has two converging lens systems: the objective and the eyepiece

hand_glass (light_microscope).definition: light microscope consisting of a single convex lens that is used to produce an enlarged image

loupe.definition: small magnifying glass (usually set in an eyepiece) used by jewelers and horologists

ultramicroscope.definition: light microscope that uses scattered light to show particles too small to see with ordinary microscopes

telescope.definition: a magnifier of images of distant objects

astronomical_telescope.definition: any telescope designed to collect and record electromagnetic radiation from cosmic sources

optical_telescope.definition: an astronomical telescope designed to collect and record light from cosmic sources

reflecting_telescope.definition: optical telescope consisting of a large concave mirror that produces an image that is magnified by the eyepiece

cassegrainian_telescope.definition: a reflecting telescope that has a paraboloidal primary mirror and a hyperboloidal secondary mirror; light is brought to a focus through an aperture in the center of the primary mirror

coude_telescope.definition: a reflecting telescope so constructed that the light is led to a plate holder or spectrograph

herschelian_telescope.definition: a reflecting telescope with the mirror slightly tilted to throw the image to the side where it can be viewed

maksutov_telescope.definition: reflecting telescope in which the aberration of the concave mirror is reduced by a meniscus lens

newtonian_telescope.definition: reflecting telescope in which the image is viewed through an eyepiece perpendicular to main axis

schmidt_telescope.definition: reflecting telescope that has plate that corrects for aberration so a wide area of sky can be photographed

refracting_telescope.definition: optical telescope that has a large convex lens that produces an image that is viewed through the eyepiece

galilean_telescope.definition: a type of refracting telescope that is no longer used in astronomy

radio_telescope.definition: astronomical telescope that picks up electromagnetic radiations in the radio-frequency range from extraterrestrial sources

radio_interferometer.definition: radio telescope that uses interference patterns from two antennas instead of a parabolic antenna

collimator (telescope).definition: a small telescope attached to a large telescope to use in setting the line of the larger one

equatorial.definition: a telescope whose mounting has only two axes of motion, one parallel to the Earth's axis and the other one at right angles to it

solar_telescope.definition: a telescope designed to make observations of the sun

transit_instrument.definition: a telescope mounted on an axis running east and west and used to time the transit of a celestial body across the meridian

microtome.definition: scientific instrument that cuts thin slices of something for microscopic examination

stroboscope.definition: scientific instrument that provides a flashing light synchronized with the periodic movement of an object; can make moving object appear stationary

tachistoscope.definition: scientific instrument used by psychologists; presents visual stimuli for brief exposures

telemeter.definition: any scientific instrument for observing events at a distance and transmitting the information back to the observer

sonograph.definition: an instrument that uses the differential transmission and reflection of ultrasonic waves in order to provide an image of a bodily organ

echocardiograph.definition: a sonograph that creates an image of the heart and its abnormalities

echoencephalograph.definition: a sonograph that creates an image of the brain and its abnormalities

clinometer.definition: an instrument used by surveyors in order to measure an angle of inclination or elevation

plane_table.definition: surveying instrument consisting of a drawing board and a ruler that are mounted on a tripod; used to sight and map topographical details

range_pole.definition: surveying instrument consisting of a straight rod painted in bands of alternate red and white each one foot wide; used for sightings by surveyors

surveyor's_level.definition: surveying instrument consisting basically of a small telescope with an attached spirit level rotating around a vertical axis; for measuring relative heights of land

abney_level.definition: a surveying instrument consisting of a spirit level and a sighting tube; used to measure the angle of inclination of a line from the observer to the target

dumpy_level.definition: a surveyor's level having a short telescope fixed to a horizontally rotating table and a spirit level

theodolite.definition: a surveying instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles, consisting of a small telescope mounted on a tripod

tachymeter.definition: a theodolite designed for rapid measurements

tracer (instrument).definition: an instrument used to make tracings

weapon.definition: any instrument or instrumentality used in fighting or hunting

missile.definition: a rocket carrying a warhead of conventional or nuclear explosives; may be ballistic or directed by remote control

air-to-air_missile.definition: a missile designed to be launched from one airplane at another

air-to-ground_missile.definition: a missile designed to be launched from an airplane at a target on the ground

ballistic_missile.definition: a missile that is guided in the first part of its flight but falls freely as it approaches target

intercontinental_ballistic_missile.definition: a ballistic missile that is capable of traveling from one continent to another

minuteman (intercontinental_ballistic_mi.definition: a strategic weapon system using a guided missile of intercontinental range; missiles are equipped with nuclear warheads and dispersed in hardened silos

guided_missile.definition: a rocket-propelled missile whose path can be controlled during flight either by radio signals or by internal homing devices

antiballistic_missile.definition: a defensive missile designed to shoot down incoming intercontinental ballistic missiles

buzz_bomb.definition: a small jet-propelled winged missile that carries a bomb

exocet.definition: a guided missile developed by the French government for use against ships

space_probe.definition: a rocket-propelled guided missile that can escape the earth's atmosphere; makes observations of the solar system that cannot be made by terrestrial observation

surface-to-air_missile.definition: a guided missile fired from land or shipboard against an airborne target

heat-seeking_missile.definition: a missile with a guidance system that directs it toward targets emitting infrared radiation (as the emissions of a jet engine)

stinger.definition: a portable low altitude surface-to-air missile system using infrared guidance and an impact fuse; fired from the shoulder

brilliant_pebble.definition: a code name for a small computerized heat-seeking missile that was supposed to intercept and destroy enemy missiles

sidewinder (missile).definition: air-to-air missile with infrared homing device

bow (weapon).definition: a weapon for shooting arrows, composed of a curved piece of resilient wood with a taut cord to propel the arrow

crossbow.definition: a bow fixed transversely on a wooden stock grooved to direct the arrow (quarrel)

cupid's_bow.definition: a curved bow with reversed curve ends

handbow.definition: a bow drawn by hand as distinguished from a crossbow

longbow.definition: a powerful wooden bow drawn by hand; usually 5-6 feet long; used in medieval England

bow_and_arrow.definition: a weapon consisting of arrows and the bow to shoot them

brass_knucks.definition: a small metal weapon; worn over the knuckles on the back of the hand

fire_ship.definition: a weapon consisting of a ship carrying explosives that is set adrift to destroy enemy ships

flamethrower.definition: a weapon that squirts ignited fuel for several yards

greek_fire.definition: a mixture used by Byzantine Greeks that was often shot at adversaries; catches fire when wetted

gun.definition: a weapon that discharges a missile at high velocity (especially from a metal tube or barrel)

air_gun.definition: a gun that propels a projectile by compressed air

bb_gun.definition: an air gun in which BBs are propelled by compressed air

antiaircraft.definition: artillery designed to shoot upward at airplanes

breechloader.definition: a gun that is loaded at the breech

automatic_firearm.definition: a firearm that reloads itself and keeps firing until the trigger is released

machine_gun.definition: a rapidly firing automatic gun (often mounted)

assault_rifle.definition: any of the automatic rifles or semiautomatic rifles with large magazines designed for military use

browning_automatic_rifle.definition: a portable .30 caliber automatic rifle operated by gas pressure and fed by cartridges from a magazine; used by United States troops in World War I and in World War II and in the Korean War

browning_machine_gun.definition: a belt-fed machine gun capable of firing more than 500 rounds per minute; used by United States troops in World War II and the Korean War

gatling_gun.definition: an early form of machine gun having several barrels that fire in sequence as they are rotated

maxim_gun.definition: an obsolete water-cooled machine gun having a single barrel

submachine_gun.definition: machine gun that is a portable automatic firearm

bren.definition: a submachine gun operated by gas pressure; used by the British in World War II

burp_gun.definition: a fully automatic pistol; a small submachine gun

kalashnikov.definition: a type of submachine gun made in Russia

light_machine_gun.definition: a submachine gun not greater than .30 millimeter

uzi.definition: a type of submachine gun that is designed and manufactured in Israel

semiautomatic_firearm.definition: an autoloader that fires only one shot at each pull of the trigger

muzzle_loader.definition: an obsolete firearm that was loaded through the muzzle

arquebus.definition: an obsolete firearm with a long barrel

flintlock (muzzle_loader).definition: a muzzle loader that had a flintlock type of gunlock

musket.definition: a muzzle-loading shoulder gun with a long barrel; formerly used by infantrymen

blunderbuss.definition: a short musket of wide bore with a flared muzzle

matchlock.definition: an early style of musket; a slow-burning wick would be lowered into a hole in the breech to ignite the charge

pistol.definition: a firearm that is held and fired with one hand

automatic_pistol.definition: a pistol that will keep firing until the ammunition is gone or the trigger is released

semiautomatic_pistol.definition: a pistol that is a semiautomatic firearm capable of loading and firing continuously

derringer.definition: a pocket pistol of large caliber with a short barrel

horse_pistol.definition: a large pistol (usually in a holster) formerly carried by horsemen

peacekeeper (pistol).definition: the pistol of a law officer in the old West

revolver.definition: a pistol with a revolving cylinder (usually having six chambers for bullets)

saturday_night_special.definition: a cheap handgun that is easily obtained

very_pistol.definition: a pistol for firing Very-light flares

repeating_firearm.definition: a firearm that can fire several rounds without reloading

mauser.definition: trademark for a repeating rifle or pistol

rifle.definition: a shoulder firearm with a long barrel and a rifled bore

sniper_rifle.definition: an extremely powerful rifle developed for the military; capable of destroying light armored vehicles and aircraft more than a mile away

dragunov.definition: a sniper rifle with a telescopic sight

riot_gun.definition: a firearm designed to disperse rioters rather than to inflict serious injury or death

shotgun.definition: firearm that is a double-barreled smoothbore shoulder weapon for firing shot at short ranges

fowling_piece.definition: a light shotgun used for fowling

smoothbore.definition: a firearm that has no rifling

gas_gun.definition: a gun that fires gas shells

minute_gun.definition: (military) gun that is discharged once every minute (usually as part of a military funeral)

quaker_gun.definition: a dummy gun or piece of artillery made usually of wood

set_gun.definition: a gun that is set to fire on any intruder that comes in contact with the wire that sets it off

whaling_gun.definition: a gun (or device resembling a gun) for discharging a projectile (especially a harpoon) at a whale

knife (weapon).definition: a weapon with a handle and blade with a sharp point

bayonet.definition: a knife that can be fixed to the end of a rifle and used as a weapon

dagger.definition: a short knife with a pointed blade used for piercing or stabbing

dirk.definition: a relatively long dagger with a straight blade

kirpan.definition: a ceremonial four-inch curved dagger that Sikh men and women are obliged to wear at all times

kris.definition: a Malayan dagger with a wavy blade

poniard.definition: a dagger with a slender blade

stiletto.definition: a small dagger with a tapered blade

khukuri.definition: a curved steel knife with a razor-sharp edge used in combat by the Gurkhas; has cultural and religious significance in Nepal

machete.definition: a large heavy knife used in Central and South America as a weapon or for cutting vegetation

shiv.definition: a knife used as a weapon

trench_knife.definition: a knife with a double-edged blade for hand-to-hand fighting

yataghan.definition: a long Turkish knife with a curved blade having a single edge

pike (weapon).definition: medieval weapon consisting of a spearhead attached to a long pole or pikestaff; superseded by the bayonet

halberd.definition: a pike fitted with an ax head

partisan (pike).definition: a pike with a long tapering double-edged blade with lateral projections; 16th and 17th centuries

vouge.definition: a kind of pike used by foot soldiers in the 14th century

projectile.definition: a weapon that is forcibly thrown or projected at a targets but is not self-propelled

arrow.definition: a projectile with a straight thin shaft and an arrowhead on one end and stabilizing vanes on the other; intended to be shot from a bow

broad_arrow.definition: an arrow with a wide barbed head

butt_shaft.definition: a blunt arrow without a barb; an arrow used for target practice

quarrel.definition: an arrow that is shot from a crossbow; has a head with four edges

boomerang.definition: a curved piece of wood; when properly thrown will return to thrower

kylie.definition: an Australian boomerang; one side flat and the other convex

bullet.definition: a projectile that is fired from a gun

dumdum.definition: a soft-nosed small-arms bullet that expands when it hits a target and causes a gaping wound

full_metal_jacket.definition: a lead bullet that is covered with a jacket of a harder metal (usually copper)

rifle_ball.definition: a bullet designed to be fired from a rifle; no longer made spherical in shape

rubber_bullet.definition: a bullet made of hard rubber; designed for use in crowd control

cannonball.definition: a solid projectile that in former times was fired from a cannon

dart.definition: a small narrow pointed missile that is thrown or shot

banderilla.definition: a decorated dart that is implanted in the neck or shoulders of the bull during a bull fight

seeker (projectile).definition: a missile equipped with a device that is attracted toward some kind of emission (heat or light or sound or radio waves)

shot (projectile).definition: a solid missile discharged from a firearm

bb.definition: a small pellet fired from an air rifle or BB gun

bird_shot.definition: small lead shot for shotgun shells

grapeshot.definition: a cluster of small projectiles fired together from a cannon to produce a hail of shot

musket_ball.definition: a solid projectile that is shot by a musket

spitball.definition: a projectile made by chewing a piece of paper and shaping it into a sphere

slasher (weapon).definition: a weapon (a sword or dagger) used for slashing

sling (weapon).definition: a simple weapon consisting of a looped strap in which a projectile is whirled and then released

spear (weapon).definition: a long pointed rod used as a tool or weapon

assegai.definition: the slender spear of the Bantu-speaking people of Africa

stun_gun.definition: a weapon designed to disable a victim temporarily by delivering a nonlethal high-voltage electric shock

sword.definition: a cutting or thrusting weapon that has a long metal blade and a hilt with a hand guard

backsword.definition: a sword with only one cutting edge

broadsword.definition: a sword with a broad blade and (usually) two cutting edges; used to cut rather than stab

claymore.definition: a large double-edged broadsword; formerly used by Scottish Highlanders

cavalry_sword.definition: a stout sword with a curved blade and thick back

scimitar.definition: a curved oriental saber; the edge is on the convex side of the blade

cutlas.definition: a short heavy curved sword with one edge; formerly used by sailors

falchion.definition: a short broad slightly convex medieval sword with a sharp point

fencing_sword.definition: a sword used in the sport of fencing

epee.definition: a fencing sword similar to a foil but with a heavier blade

foil (fencing_sword).definition: a light slender flexible sword tipped by a button

saber.definition: a fencing sword with a v-shaped blade and a slightly curved handle

rapier.definition: a straight sword with a narrow blade and two edges

tomahawk.definition: weapon consisting of a fighting ax; used by North American Indians

weapon_of_mass_destruction.definition: a weapon that kills or injures civilian as well as military personnel (nuclear and chemical and biological weapons)

bioweapon.definition: any weapon usable in biological warfare

aflatoxin.definition: a potent carcinogen from the fungus Aspergillus; can be produced and stored for use as a bioweapon

botulin.definition: potent bacterial toxin produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum that causes botulism; can be used as a bioweapon

staphylococcal_enterotoxin_b.definition: a form of staphylococcal enterotoxin that has been used as an incapacitating agent in biological warfare

chemical_weapon.definition: chemical substances that can be delivered using munitions and dispersal devices to cause death or severe harm to people and animals and plants

pepper_spray.definition: a nonlethal aerosol spray made with the pepper derivative oleoresin capiscum; used to cause temporary blindness and incapacitate an attacker; also used as a bear deterrent

poison_gas.definition: a gas that is poisonous to breath or contact; used in chemical warfare

mustard_gas.definition: a toxic war gas with sulfide based compounds that raises blisters and attacks the eyes and lungs; there is no known antidote

nerve_gas.definition: a toxic gas that is inhaled or absorbed through the skin and has harmful effects on the nervous and respiratory system

organophosphate_nerve_agent.definition: any of a series of nerve agents containing organophosphate compounds first synthesized by German chemists in 1936; in World War II the Germans tested them in concentration camps but not on the battlefield; Iraq is alleged to have used them against Iran and against the Kurds

sarin.definition: a highly toxic chemical nerve agent that inhibits the activity of cholinesterase

soman.definition: a nerve agent easily absorbed into the body; a lethal cholinesterase inhibitor that is highly toxic when inhaled

tabun.definition: the first known nerve agent, synthesized by German chemists in 1936; a highly toxic combustible liquid that is soluble in organic solvents and is used as a nerve gas in chemical warfare

vx_gas.definition: a highly lethal nerve agent used in chemical warfare; a toxic liquid that penetrates the skin or lungs to disrupt the nervous system and stop respiration; in combat VX gas is deployed by detonating a container over the target area and can persist in the environment up to several weeks after release

tear_gas.definition: a gas that makes the eyes fill with tears but does not damage them; used in dispersing crowds

chloroacetophenone.definition: a tear gas that is weaker than CS gas but lasts longer

mace.definition: (trademark) a liquid that temporarily disables a person; prepared as an aerosol and sprayed in the face, it irritates the eyes and causes dizziness and immobilization

chlorobenzylidenemalononitrile.definition: a tear gas that is stronger than CN gas but wears off faster; can be deployed by grenades or cluster bombs; can cause skin burns and fatal pulmonary edema

nitrochloromethane.definition: gaseous form of chloropicrin used as tear gas

high_explosive.definition: a powerful chemical explosive that produces gas at a very high rate

disrupting_explosive.definition: a high explosive that is used to damage the target that is under attack

nuclear_weapon.definition: a weapon of mass destruction whose explosive power derives from a nuclear reaction

whip (instrument).definition: an instrument with a handle and a flexible lash that is used for whipping

cat-o'-nine-tails.definition: a whip with nine knotted cords

cowhide.definition: a heavy flexible whip braided from leather made from the hide of a cow

buggy_whip.definition: a horsewhip once used by a driver of a buggy

knout.definition: a whip with a lash of leather thongs twisted with wire; used for flogging prisoners

quirt.definition: whip with a leather thong at the end

riding_crop.definition: a short whip with a thong at the end and a handle for opening gates

scourge.definition: a whip used to inflict punishment (often used for pedantic humor)

strap (whip).definition: whip consisting of a strip of leather used in flogging

tawse.definition: a leather strap for punishing children

interlock.definition: a device that prevents an automotive engine from starting

interrupter.definition: a device for automatically interrupting an electric current

jig (device).definition: a device that holds a piece of machine work and guides the tools operating on it

key (device).definition: metal device shaped in such a way that when it is inserted into the appropriate lock the lock's mechanism can be rotated

ignition_key.definition: a key that operates the ignition switch of an automotive engine

latchkey.definition: key for raising or drawing back a latch or opening an outside door

skeleton_key.definition: a passkey with much of the bit filed away so that it can open different locks

keyboard (device).definition: device consisting of a set of keys on a piano or organ or typewriter or typesetting machine or computer or the like

piano_keyboard.definition: a bank of keys on a musical instrument

typewriter_keyboard.definition: a keyboard for manually entering characters to be printed

qwerty_keyboard.definition: the standard typewriter keyboard; the keys for Q, W, E, R, T, and Y are the first six from the left on the top row of letter keys

kinetoscope.definition: a device invented by Edison that gave an impression of movement as an endless loop of film moved continuously over a light source with a rapid shutter; precursor of the modern motion picture

knocker (device).definition: a device (usually metal and ornamental) attached by a hinge to a door

lift (device).definition: a device worn in a shoe or boot to make the wearer look taller or to correct a shortened leg

lifting_device.definition: a device for lifting heavy loads

davit.definition: a crane-like device (usually one of a pair) for suspending or lowering equipment (as a lifeboat)

derrick (crane).definition: a simple crane having lifting tackle slung from a boom

transporter (crane).definition: a crane for moving material with dispatch as in loading and unloading ships

dumbwaiter.definition: a small elevator used to convey food (or other goods) from one floor of a building to another

freight_elevator.definition: an elevator designed for carrying freight

paternoster.definition: a type of lift having a chain of open compartments that move continually in an endless loop so that (agile) passengers can step on or off at each floor

hoist.definition: lifting device for raising heavy or cumbersome objects

block_and_tackle.definition: pulley blocks with associated rope or cable

headgear (hoist).definition: the hoist at the pithead of a mine

wheel_and_axle.definition: hoist so arranged that a rope unwinding from a wheel is wound onto a cylindrical drum or shaft coaxial with the wheel

winch.definition: lifting device consisting of a horizontal cylinder turned by a crank on which a cable or rope winds

capstan.definition: a windlass rotated in a horizontal plane around a vertical axis; used on ships for weighing anchor or raising heavy sails

yarder.definition: a winch (or system of winches) powered by an engine and used to haul logs from a stump to a landing or to a skid road

lighter.definition: a device for lighting or igniting fuel or charges or fires

cigar_lighter.definition: a lighter for cigars or cigarettes

fuse (lighter).definition: any igniter that is used to initiate the burning of a propellant

safety_fuse.definition: a slow-burning fuse consisting of a tube or cord filled or saturated with combustible matter; used to ignite detonators from a distance

time-fuse.definition: a fuse made to burn for a given time (especially to explode a bomb)

fusee (match).definition: a friction match with a large head that will stay alight in the wind

kitchen_match.definition: a wooden friction match that will light on any granular surface; useful to light wood or gas stoves

safety_match.definition: a paper match that strikes only on a specially prepared surface

slow_match.definition: match or fuse made to burn slowly and evenly

machine (device).definition: any mechanical or electrical device that transmits or modifies energy to perform or assist in the performance of human tasks

assembly (machine).definition: a group of machine parts that fit together to form a self-contained unit

sub-assembly.definition: a unit assembled separately but designed to fit with other units in a manufactured product

weldment.definition: an assembly of parts welded together

bagger.definition: a machine for putting objects or substances into bags

calculator (machine).definition: a small machine that is used for mathematical calculations

abacus (calculator).definition: a calculator that performs arithmetic functions by manually sliding counters on rods or in grooves

adding_machine.definition: a calculator that performs simple arithmetic functions

counter (calculator).definition: a calculator that keeps a record of the number of times something happens

pulse_counter.definition: an electronic counter that counts the number of electric pulses

scaler.definition: an electronic pulse counter used to count pulses that occur too rapidly to be recorded individually

hand_calculator.definition: a calculator small enough to hold in the hand or carry in a pocket

napier's_bones.definition: a set of graduated rods formerly used to do multiplication and division by a method invented by John Napier

quipu.definition: calculator consisting of a cord with attached cords; used by ancient Peruvians for calculating and keeping records

calender.definition: a machine that smooths or glazes paper or cloth by pressing it between plates or passing it through rollers

cash_machine.definition: an unattended machine (outside some banks) that dispenses money when a personal coded card is used

comber (machine).definition: a machine that separates and straightens the fibers of cotton or wool

computer.definition: a machine for performing calculations automatically

analog_computer.definition: a computer that represents information by variable quantities (e.g., positions or voltages)

differential_analyzer.definition: an analog computer designed to solve differential equations

slide_rule.definition: analog computer consisting of a handheld instrument used for rapid calculations; have been replaced by pocket calculators

digital_computer.definition: a computer that represents information by numerical (binary) digits

bulletin_board_system.definition: a computer that is running software that allows users to leave messages and access information of general interest

file_server.definition: (computer science) a digital computer that provides workstations on a network with controlled access to shared resources

dedicated_file_server.definition: (computer science) a file server that can be used only as a file server

non-dedicated_file_server.definition: (computer science) a file server that can be used simultaneously as a workstation

mainframe.definition: a large digital computer serving 100-400 users and occupying a special air-conditioned room

supercomputer.definition: a mainframe computer that is one of the most powerful available at a given time

minicomputer.definition: a digital computer of medium size

multiprocessor.definition: a computer that uses two or more processing units under integrated control

personal_computer.definition: a small digital computer based on a microprocessor and designed to be used by one person at a time

desktop_computer.definition: a personal computer small enough to fit conveniently in an individual workspace

portable_computer.definition: a personal computer that can easily be carried by hand

briefcase_computer.definition: a portable computer housed in a box that resembles a briefcase

hand-held_computer.definition: a portable battery-powered computer small enough to be carried in your pocket

laptop.definition: a portable computer small enough to use in your lap

planner (notebook).definition: a notebook for recording appointments and things to be done, etc.

von_neumann_machine.definition: any digital computer incorporating the ideas of stored programs and serial counters that were proposed in 1946 by von Neumann and his colleagues

workstation.definition: a desktop digital computer that is conventionally considered to be more powerful than a microcomputer

home_computer.definition: a computer intended for use in the home

node (computer).definition: (computer science) any computer that is hooked up to a computer network

number_cruncher (computer).definition: a computer capable of performing a large number of mathematical operations per second

pari-mutuel_machine.definition: computer that registers bets and divides the total amount bet among those who won

predictor.definition: a computer for controlling antiaircraft fire that computes the position of an aircraft at the instant of a shell's arrival

server (computer).definition: (computer science) a computer that provides client stations with access to files and printers as shared resources to a computer network

turing_machine.definition: a hypothetical computer with an infinitely long memory tape

web_site.definition: a computer connected to the internet that maintains a series of web pages on the World Wide Web

chat_room.definition: a site on the internet where a number of users can communicate in real time (typically one dedicated to a particular topic)

portal_site.definition: a site that the owner positions as an entrance to other sites on the internet

concrete_mixer.definition: a machine with a large revolving drum in which cement is mixed with other materials to make concrete

corker.definition: a machine that is used to put corks in bottles

cotton_gin.definition: a machine that separates the seeds from raw cotton fibers

decoder (machine).definition: a machine that converts a coded text into ordinary language

cultivator.definition: a farm implement used to break up the surface of the soil (for aeration and weed control and conservation of moisture)

harrow.definition: a cultivator that pulverizes or smooths the soil

disk_harrow.definition: a harrow with a series of disks set on edge at an angle

harvester (farm_machine).definition: farm machine that gathers a food crop from the fields

binder (harvester).definition: a machine that cuts grain and binds it in sheaves

combine.definition: harvester that heads and threshes and cleans grain while moving across the field

header (harvester).definition: a machine that cuts the heads off grain and moves them into a wagon

haymaker.definition: a farm machine that treats hay to cause more rapid and even drying

thresher (farm_machine).definition: a farm machine for separating seeds or grain from the husks and straw

franking_machine.definition: a machine that automatically stamps letters or packages passing through it and computes the total charge

hop-picker.definition: a machine used for picking hops

machine_tool.definition: a powered machine for cutting or shaping or finishing metals or other materials

drill_press.definition: a machine tool with a separate, upright stand; an electric drill is pressed into the work automatically or with a hand lever

grinder.definition: a machine tool that polishes metal

shaper.definition: a machine tool for shaping metal or wood

lathe.definition: machine tool for shaping metal or wood; the workpiece turns about a horizontal axis against a fixed tool

miller (shaper).definition: machine tool in which metal that is secured to a carriage is fed against rotating cutters that shape it

mill.definition: machinery that processes materials by grinding or crushing

cider_mill.definition: mill that extracts juice from apples to make apple cider

coffee_mill.definition: a mill that grinds roasted coffee beans

flour_mill.definition: a mill for grinding grain into flour

gristmill.definition: a mill for grinding grain (especially the customer's own grain)

quern.definition: a primitive stone mill for grinding corn by hand

treadmill (mill).definition: a mill that is powered by men or animals walking on a circular belt or climbing steps

water_mill.definition: a mill powered by a water wheel

windmill (mill).definition: a mill that is powered by the wind

milking_machine.definition: machine consisting of a suction apparatus for milking cows mechanically

motor.definition: machine that converts other forms of energy into mechanical energy and so imparts motion

electric_motor.definition: a motor that converts electricity to mechanical work

starter (electric_motor).definition: an electric motor for starting an engine

kick_starter.definition: a starter (as on a motorcycle) that is activated with the foot and the weight of the body

self-starter (starter).definition: an electric starting motor that automatically starts an internal-combustion engine

synchronous_motor.definition: electric motor in which the speed of rotation is proportional to the frequency of the A.C. power

wiper_motor.definition: electric motor that moves the windshield wiper

engine (motor).definition: motor that converts thermal energy to mechanical work

aircraft_engine.definition: the engine that powers and aircraft

automobile_engine.definition: the engine that propels an automobile

auxiliary_engine.definition: (nautical) a small engine (as one used on board ships to operate a windlass)

generator (engine).definition: engine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction

alternator.definition: an old term for an electric generator that produces alternating current (especially in automobiles)

dynamo.definition: generator consisting of a coil (the armature) that rotates between the poles of an electromagnet (the field magnet) causing a current to flow in the armature

magneto.definition: a small dynamo with a secondary winding that produces a high voltage enabling a spark to jump between the poles of a spark plug in a gasoline engine

turbogenerator.definition: generator consisting of a steam turbine coupled to an electric generator for the production of electric power

windmill (generator).definition: generator that extracts usable energy from winds

heat_engine.definition: any engine that makes use of heat to do work

external-combustion_engine.definition: a heat engine in which ignition occurs outside the chamber (cylinder or turbine) in which heat is converted to mechanical energy

steam_engine.definition: external-combustion engine in which heat is used to raise steam which either turns a turbine or forces a piston to move up and down in a cylinder

internal-combustion_engine.definition: a heat engine in which combustion occurs inside the engine rather than in a separate furnace; heat expands a gas that either moves a piston or turns a gas turbine

diesel.definition: an internal-combustion engine that burns heavy oil

four-stroke_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine in which an explosive mixture is drawn into the cylinder on the first stroke and is compressed and ignited on the second stroke; work is done on the third stroke and the products of combustion are exhausted on the fourth stroke

gas_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine similar to a gasoline engine but using natural gas instead of gasoline vapor

gasoline_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine that burns gasoline; most automobiles are driven by gasoline engines

put-put.definition: a small gasoline engine (as on motor boat)

outboard_motor.definition: internal-combustion engine that mounts at stern of small boat

radial_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine having cylinders arranged radially around a central crankcase

reciprocating_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine in which the crankshaft is turned by pistons moving up and down in cylinders

rotary_engine.definition: an internal-combustion engine in which power is transmitted directly to rotating components

turbine.definition: rotary engine in which the kinetic energy of a moving fluid is converted into mechanical energy by causing a bladed rotor to rotate

gas_turbine.definition: turbine that converts the chemical energy of a liquid fuel into mechanical energy by internal combustion; gaseous products of the fuel (which is burned in compressed air) are expanded through a turbine

hydroelectric_turbine.definition: turbine consisting of a large and efficient version of a water wheel used to drive an electric generator

impulse_turbine.definition: a turbine that is driven by jets direct against the blades

reaction_turbine.definition: a turbine with blades arranged to develop torque from gradual decrease of steam pressure from inlet to exhaust

steam_turbine.definition: turbine in which steam strikes blades and makes them turn

wind_turbine.definition: a turbine that is driven by the wind

wankel_engine.definition: a rotary engine that is a four-stroke internal-combustion engine without reciprocating parts

valve-in-head_engine.definition: internal-combustion engine having both inlet and exhaust valves located in the cylinder head

reaction-propulsion_engine.definition: a jet or rocket engine based on a form of aerodynamic propulsion in which the vehicle emits a high-speed stream

ion_engine.definition: a type of reaction-propulsion engine to propel rockets in space; a stream of positive ions is accelerated to a high velocity by an electric field

jet_engine.definition: a gas turbine produces a stream of hot gas that propels a jet plane by reaction propulsion

fanjet (jet_engine).definition: a jet engine in which a fan driven by a turbine provides extra air to the burner and gives extra thrust

ramjet.definition: a simple type of jet engine; must be launched at high speed

rocket (jet_engine).definition: a jet engine containing its own propellant and driven by reaction propulsion

booster (rocket).definition: the first stage of a multistage rocket

nuclear_rocket.definition: a rocket engine in which a nuclear reactor is used to heat a propellant

retrorocket.definition: a small rocket engine on a larger rocket or spacecraft that is fired to slow or alter its course

space_rocket.definition: a rocket powerful enough to travel into outer space

thruster.definition: a small rocket engine that provides the thrust needed to maneuver a spacecraft

stepper (motor).definition: a motor (especially an electric motor) that moves or rotates in small discrete steps

perpetual_motion_machine.definition: a machine that can continue to do work indefinitely without drawing energy from some external source; impossible under the law of conservation of energy

pile_driver.definition: a machine that drives piling into the ground

backhoe.definition: an excavator whose shovel bucket is attached to a hinged boom and is drawn backward to move earth

dredge.definition: a power shovel to remove material from a channel or riverbed

steam_shovel.definition: a power shovel that is driven by steam

flatbed_press.definition: a printing press where the type is carried on a flat bed under a cylinder that holds paper and rolls over the type

rotary_press.definition: a printing press for printing from a revolving cylinder

standing_press.definition: a large printing press that exerts pressure vertically

cheese_press.definition: a press for shaping cheese curd

ciderpress.definition: a press that is used to extract the juice from apples

garlic_press.definition: a press for extracting juice from garlic

hydraulic_press.definition: press in which a force applied by a piston to a small area is transmitted through water to another piston having a large area

punch_press.definition: a power driven press used to shape metal parts

bench_press.definition: a small punch press mounted on a workbench

winepress.definition: a press that is used to extract the juice from grapes

addressing_machine.definition: a printer that automatically prints addresses on letters for mailing

character_printer.definition: a printer that prints a single character at a time

daisywheel_printer.definition: a printer that uses a daisy print wheel

teletypewriter.definition: a character printer connected to a telegraph that operates like a typewriter

ticker.definition: a character printer that automatically prints stock quotations on ticker tape

typewriter.definition: hand-operated character printer for printing written messages one character at a time

electric_typewriter.definition: a typewriter powered by an electric motor

portable.definition: a small light typewriter; usually with a case in which it can be carried

stenograph.definition: a machine for typewriting shorthand characters

electrostatic_printer.definition: a printer that uses an electric charge to deposit toner on paper

laser_printer.definition: electrostatic printer that focuses a laser beam to form images that are transferred to paper electrostatically

impact_printer.definition: a printer that prints by mechanical impacts

bar_printer.definition: an impact printer that uses a bar to carry the type slugs

chain_printer.definition: an impact printer that carries the type slugs by links of a revolving chain

line_printer.definition: printer that serves as an output device on a computer; prints a whole line of characters at a time

drum_printer.definition: a line printer in which the type is mounted on a rotating drum that contains a full character set for each printing position

page_printer.definition: a printer that prints one page at a time

xerographic_printer.definition: a page printer that uses the xerographic process

thermal_printer.definition: a printer that produces characters by applying heat to special paper that is sensitive to heat

typesetting_machine.definition: a printer that sets textual material in type

linotype.definition: a typesetting machine operated from a keyboard that casts an entire line as a single slug of metal

monotype.definition: a typesetting machine operated from a keyboard that sets separate characters

record_player.definition: machine in which rotating records cause a stylus to vibrate and the vibrations are amplified acoustically or electronically

gramophone.definition: an antique record player; the sound of the vibrating needle is amplified acoustically

jukebox.definition: a cabinet containing an automatic record player; records are played by inserting a coin

self-feeder.definition: a machine that automatically provides a supply of some material

simulator.definition: a machine that simulates an environment for the purpose of training or research

flight_simulator.definition: simulator consisting of a machine on the ground that simulates the conditions of flying a plane

link_trainer.definition: an early form of flight simulator

slicer (machine).definition: a machine for cutting; usually with a revolving blade

slot_machine.definition: a machine that is operated by the insertion of a coin in a slot

slot (slot_machine).definition: a slot machine that is used for gambling

fruit_machine.definition: a coin-operated gambling machine that produces random combinations of symbols (usually pictures of different fruits) on rotating dials; certain combinations win money for the player

vending_machine.definition: a slot machine for selling goods

automat (vending_machine).definition: a vending machine from which you can get food

snow_thrower.definition: a machine that removes snow by scooping it up and throwing it forcefully through a chute

sorter (machine).definition: a machine for sorting things (such as punched cards or letters) into classes

mailsorter.definition: a sorter for sorting mail according to the address

stamp (machine).definition: machine consisting of a heavy bar that moves vertically for pounding or crushing ores

staple_gun.definition: a hand-held machine for driving staples home

stapler.definition: a machine that inserts staples into sheets of paper in order to fasten them together

sewing_machine.definition: a textile machine used as a home appliance for sewing

serger.definition: a sewing machine that overcasts the raw edges of a fabric with a V-shaped stitch

knitting_machine.definition: a textile machine that makes knitted fabrics

loom.definition: a textile machine for weaving yarn into a textile

figure_loom.definition: a loom for weaving figured fabrics

high-warp_loom.definition: a handloom in which the warp is carried vertically; for weaving tapestry

low-warp-loom.definition: a handloom in which the warp is carried horizontally; for weaving tapestry

spinning_jenny.definition: an early spinning machine with multiple spindles

spinning_wheel.definition: a small domestic spinning machine with a single spindle that is driven by hand or foot

throstle.definition: a spinning machine formerly used to twist and wind fibers of cotton or wool continuously

push-down_storage.definition: a storage device that handles data so that the next item to be retrieved is the item most recently stored (LIFO)

recording.definition: a storage device on which information (sounds or images) have been recorded

compact_disk.definition: a digitally encoded recording on an optical disk that is smaller than a phonograph record; played back by a laser

cd-rom.definition: a compact disk that is used with a computer (rather than with an audio system); a large amount of digital information can be stored and accessed but it cannot be altered by the user

audio_cd.definition: compact discs used to reproduce sound (voice and music)

cd-r.definition: a compact disc on which you can write only once and thereafter is read-only memory

cover.definition: a recording of a song that was first recorded or made popular by somebody else

phonograph_record.definition: sound recording consisting of a disk with a continuous groove; used to reproduce music by rotating while a phonograph needle tracks in the groove

lp.definition: a long-playing phonograph record; designed to be played at 33.3 rpm

seventy-eight.definition: a shellac based phonograph record that played at 78 revolutions per minute

soundtrack.definition: sound recording on a narrow strip of a motion picture film

dubbing.definition: a new soundtrack that is added to a film

laugh_track.definition: prerecorded laughter added to the soundtrack of a radio or television show

talking_book.definition: sound recording of someone reading a book; frequently used by blind people

tape (recording).definition: a recording made on magnetic tape

digital_audiotape.definition: a digital tape recording of sound

transcription.definition: a sound or television recording (e.g., from a broadcast to a tape recording)

video_recording.definition: a recording of both the visual and audible components (especially one containing a recording of a movie or television program)

videotape (tape).definition: a video recording made on magnetic tape

register (memory_device).definition: (computer science) memory device that is the part of computer memory that has a specific address and that is used to hold information of a specific kind

accumulator.definition: (computer science) a register that has a built-in adder that adds an input number to the contents of the register

index_register.definition: (computer science) a register used to determine the address of an operand

shift_register.definition: (computer science) register in which all bits can be shifted one or more positions to the left or to the right

musical_instrument.definition: any of various devices or contrivances that can be used to produce musical tones or sounds

barrel_organ.definition: a musical instrument that makes music by rotation of a cylinder studded with pegs

bass (musical_instrument).definition: the member with the lowest range of a family of musical instruments

calliope.definition: a musical instrument consisting of a series of steam whistles played from a keyboard

electronic_instrument.definition: a musical instrument that generates sounds electronically

electric_organ.definition: (music) an electronic simulation of a pipe organ

theremin.definition: an electronic musical instrument; melodies can be played by moving the right hand between two rods that serve as antennas to control pitch; the left hand controls phrasing

jew's_harp.definition: a small lyre-shaped musical instrument that is placed between the teeth and played by twanging a wire tongue while changing the shape of the mouth cavity

keyboard_instrument.definition: a musical instrument that is played by means of a keyboard

celesta.definition: a musical instrument consisting of graduated steel plates that are struck by hammers activated by a keyboard

percussion_instrument.definition: a musical instrument in which the sound is produced by one object striking another

chime.definition: a percussion instrument consisting of a set of tuned bells that are struck with a hammer; used as an orchestral instrument

carillon.definition: set of bells hung in a bell tower

handbell.definition: a bell that is held in the hand

high-hat_cymbal.definition: cymbals that are operated by a foot pedal

bass_drum.definition: a large drum with two heads; makes a sound of indefinite but very low pitch

tabor.definition: a small drum with one head of soft calfskin

tambourine.definition: a shallow drum with a single drumhead and with metallic disks in the sides

tenor_drum.definition: any of various drums with small heads

timbrel.definition: small hand drum similar to a tambourine; formerly carried by itinerant jugglers

glockenspiel.definition: a percussion instrument consisting of a set of graduated metal bars mounted on a frame and played with small hammers

gong.definition: a percussion instrument consisting of a metal plate that is struck with a softheaded drumstick

marimba.definition: a percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators; played with small mallets

triangle (percussion_instrument).definition: a percussion instrument consisting of a metal bar bent in the shape of an open triangle

stringed_instrument.definition: a musical instrument in which taut strings provide the source of sound

clavichord.definition: an early stringed instrument like a piano but with more delicate sound

clavier.definition: a stringed instrument that has a keyboard

piano.definition: a keyboard instrument that is played by depressing keys that cause hammers to strike tuned strings and produce sounds

grand_piano.definition: a piano with the strings on a horizontal harp-shaped frame; usually supported by three legs

concert_grand.definition: a grand piano suitable for concert performances

mechanical_piano.definition: a mechanically operated piano that uses a roll of perforated paper to activate the keys

upright (piano).definition: a piano with a vertical sounding board

spinet (upright).definition: a small and compactly built upright piano

banjo.definition: a stringed instrument of the guitar family that has long neck and circular body

bowed_stringed_instrument.definition: stringed instruments that are played with a bow

cello.definition: a large stringed instrument; seated player holds it upright while playing

viol.definition: any of a family of bowed stringed instruments that preceded the violin family

viola_d'amore.definition: viol that is the tenor of the viol family

guarnerius.definition: a violin made by a member of the Guarneri family

lyre.definition: a harp used by ancient Greeks for accompaniment

lute.definition: chordophone consisting of a plucked instrument having a pear-shaped body, a usually bent neck, and a fretted fingerboard

mandolin.definition: a stringed instrument related to the lute, usually played with a plectrum

guitar.definition: a stringed instrument usually having six strings; played by strumming or plucking

dulcimer (zither).definition: a trapezoidal zither whose metal strings are struck with light hammers

saxhorn.definition: any of a family of brass wind instruments that resemble a bugle with valves

sackbut.definition: a medieval musical instrument resembling a trombone

american_organ.definition: a free-reed instrument in which air is drawn in through reeds by suction bellows

bandoneon.definition: a type of concertina popular in South America

harmonium.definition: a free-reed instrument in which air is forced through the reeds by bellows

kazoo.definition: a toy wind instrument that has a membrane that makes a sound when you hum into the mouthpiece

ocarina.definition: egg-shaped terra cotta wind instrument with a mouthpiece and finger holes

organ_pipe.definition: the flues and stops on a pipe organ

dulciana.definition: the organ stop having a tone of soft sweet string quality

flue_stop.definition: an organ stop with the tone of a flue pipe

reed_stop.definition: an organ stop with the tone of a reed instrument
