reed_pipe.definition: organ pipe with a vibrating reed

bagpipe.definition: a tubular wind instrument; the player blows air into a bag and squeezes it out through the drone

musette.definition: a small bagpipe formerly popular in France

chanter.definition: reed pipe with finger holes on which the melody is played

panpipe.definition: a primitive wind instrument consisting of several parallel pipes bound together

pitch_pipe.definition: a small pipe sounding a tone of standard frequency; used to establish the starting pitch for unaccompanied singing

post_horn.definition: wind instrument used by postilions of the 18th and 19th centuries

woodwind.definition: any wind instrument other than the brass instruments

beating-reed_instrument.definition: a musical instrument that sounds by means of a vibrating reed

double-reed_instrument.definition: a woodwind that has a pair of joined reeds that vibrate together

bassoon.definition: a double-reed instrument; the tenor of the oboe family

contrabassoon.definition: the bassoon that is the largest instrument in the oboe family

tenoroon.definition: a tenor bassoon; pitched a fifth higher than the ordinary bassoon

oboe_da_caccia.definition: an alto oboe; precursor of the English horn

free-reed.definition: a reed that does not fit closely over the aperture

clarinet.definition: a single-reed instrument with a straight tube

bass_clarinet.definition: a large clarinet whose range is an octave below the B-flat clarinet

sax.definition: a single-reed woodwind with a conical bore

piccolo.definition: a small flute; pitched an octave above the standard flute

nest_egg.definition: device consisting of an artificial egg left in a nest to induce hens to lay their eggs in it

biprism.definition: an optical device for obtaining interference fringes

camera_lucida.definition: an optical device consisting of an attachment that enables an observer to view simultaneously the image and a drawing surface for sketching it

finder (optical_device).definition: optical device that helps a user to find the target of interest

anastigmat.definition: compound lens or lens system designed to be free of astigmatism and able to form approximately point images

anastigmatic_lens.definition: a lens designed to correct astigmatism

camera_lens.definition: a lens that focuses the image in a camera

closeup_lens.definition: a photographic lens with a short focal length used to take pictures at short ranges

portrait_lens.definition: a compound camera lens with a relatively high aperture

telephoto_lens.definition: a camera lens that magnifies the image

compound_lens.definition: a lens system consisting of two or more lenses on the same axis

abbe_condenser.definition: a condenser having 2 or 3 lenses with wide aperture for use in microscopes

contact (lens).definition: a thin curved glass or plastic lens designed to fit over the cornea in order to correct vision or to deliver medication

converging_lens.definition: lens such that a beam of light passing through it is brought to a point or focus

crown_lens.definition: a lens made of optical crown glass

nicol_prism.definition: optical device that produces plane-polarized light

polarimeter.definition: an optical device used to measure the rotation of the plane of vibration of polarized light

prism.definition: optical device having a triangular shape and made of glass or quartz; used to deviate a beam or invert an image

erecting_prism.definition: a right-angled optical prism used to turn an inverted image upright

projector (optical_device).definition: an optical device for projecting a beam of light

rochon_prism.definition: optical device that produces plane-polarized ultraviolet light

stereoscope.definition: an optical device for viewing stereoscopic photographs

viewer.definition: an optical device for viewing photographic transparencies

override.definition: a manually operated device to correct the operation of an automatic device

paper_feed.definition: a device for inserting sheets of paper into a printer or typewriter

peeler (device).definition: a device for peeling vegetables or fruits

pick (device).definition: a small thin device (of metal or plastic or ivory) used to pluck a stringed instrument

guitar_pick.definition: a plectrum used to pluck a guitar

prod.definition: a pointed instrument that is used to prod into a state of motion

ankus.definition: an elephant goad with a sharp spike and a hook

spur.definition: a sharp prod fixed to a rider's heel and used to urge a horse onward

prompter (device).definition: a device that displays words for people to read

pull.definition: a device used for pulling something

bellpull.definition: a handle or cord that is pulled to ring a doorbell or a servant's bell etc.

mirror.definition: polished surface that forms images by reflecting light

car_mirror.definition: a mirror that the driver of a car can use

outside_mirror.definition: car mirror that reflects the view at side and behind car

rearview_mirror.definition: car mirror that reflects the view out of the rear window

cheval_glass.definition: a full length mirror mounted in a frame in which it can be tilted

hand_glass (mirror).definition: a mirror intended to be held in the hand

looking_glass.definition: a mirror; usually a ladies' dressing mirror

pier_glass.definition: a large mirror between two windows

speculum (mirror).definition: a mirror (especially one made of polished metal) for use in an optical instrument

parabolic_reflector.definition: a concave reflector used to produce a parallel beam when the source is placed at its focus or to focus an incoming parallel beam

parabolic_mirror.definition: a parabolic reflector for light radiation

solar_dish.definition: a concave mirror that concentrates the rays of the sun; can produce high temperatures

release (device).definition: a device that when pressed will release part of a mechanism

remote_control.definition: a device that can be used to control a machine or apparatus from a distance

reset.definition: device for resetting instruments or controls

seat_belt.definition: a safety belt used in a car or plane to hold you in your seat in case of an accident

airbrake (restraint).definition: a small parachute or articulated flap to reduce the speed of an aircraft

band (restraint).definition: a restraint put around something to hold it together

collet (band).definition: a band or collar that holds an individual stone in a jewelry setting

ligature (band).definition: a metal band used to attach a reed to the mouthpiece of a clarinet or saxophone

withe (band).definition: band or rope made of twisted twigs or stems

hand_brake.definition: a brake operated by hand; usually operates by mechanical linkage

airbrake (power_brake).definition: a vehicular brake that operates by compressed air; especially for heavy vehicles

brake_pad.definition: one of the pads that apply friction to both sides of the brake disk

brake_shoe.definition: a restraint provided when the brake linings are moved hydraulically against the brake drum to retard the wheel's rotation

catch (restraint).definition: a restraint that checks the motion of something

doorstop.definition: a stop that keeps open doors from moving

tripper (catch).definition: a catch mechanism that acts as a switch

chain (restraint).definition: anything that acts as a restraint

catch (fastener).definition: a fastener that fastens or locks a door or window

hood_latch.definition: a catch that holds the hood of a car shut

hook (catch).definition: a catch for locking a door

latch (catch).definition: catch for fastening a door or gate; a bar that can be lowered or slid into a groove

clasp.definition: a fastener (as a buckle or hook) that is used to hold two things together

clinch.definition: the flattened part of a nail or bolt or rivet

walkie-talkie.definition: small portable radio link (receiver and transmitter)

telecommunication_system.definition: a communication system for communicating at a distance

surveillance_system.definition: a closed-circuit television system used to maintain close observation of a person or group

color_television.definition: a television that transmits images in color

telephone_system.definition: a communication system that transmits sound between distant points

perfume.definition: a toiletry that emits and diffuses a fragrant odor

scaling_ladder.definition: a ladder used to scale walls (as in an attack)

sea_ladder.definition: (nautical) ladder to be lowered over a ship's side for coming aboard

accommodation_ladder.definition: (nautical) a portable ladder hung over the side of a vessel to give access to small boats alongside

step_ladder.definition: a folding portable ladder hinged at the top

watercourse.definition: a conduit through which water flows

canal.definition: long and narrow strip of water made for boats or for irrigation

cut (canal).definition: a canal made by erosion or excavation

industrial_watercourse.definition: a canal that is operated by one or more industries

raceway.definition: a canal for a current of water

ship_canal.definition: a canal large enough for seagoing vessels

flume.definition: watercourse that consists of an open artificial chute filled with water for power or for carrying logs

headrace.definition: a waterway that feeds water to a mill or water wheel or turbine

tailrace.definition: a watercourse that carries water away from a mill or water wheel or turbine

bob (weight).definition: a hanging weight, especially a metal ball on a string

kite_tail.definition: a bob on a kite to provide balance

plumb_bob.definition: the metal bob of a plumb line

sounding_lead.definition: a metal bob at the end of a sounding line

counterweight.definition: a weight that balances another weight

sash_weight.definition: a counterweight for a sliding sash

tare (counterweight).definition: (chemical analysis) a counterweight used in chemical analysis; consists of an empty container that counterbalances the weight of the container holding chemicals

load (weight).definition: weight to be borne or conveyed

dead_load.definition: a constant load on a structure (e.g. a bridge) due to the weight of the supported structure itself

live_load.definition: a variable load on a structure (e.g. a bridge) such as moving traffic

millstone (load).definition: any load that is difficult to carry

makeweight (weight).definition: a weight added to the scale to reach a required weight

paperweight.definition: a weight used to hold down a stack of papers

sinker.definition: a weight that sinks (as to hold nets or fishing lines under water)

assembly (whole).definition: a unit consisting of components that have been fitted together

congener.definition: a whole (a thing or person) of the same kind or category as another

item.definition: a whole individual unit; especially when included in a list or collection

custom-made.definition: an item made to the customer's specifications

disposable.definition: an item that can be disposed of after it has been used

piece (item).definition: an item that is an instance of some type

biont.definition: a discrete unit of living matter

cell (living_thing).definition: (biology) the basic structural and functional unit of all organisms; they may exist as independent units of life (as in monads) or may form colonies or tissues as in higher plants and animals

akaryocyte.definition: a cell without a nucleus (as an erythrocyte)

archespore.definition: primitive cell or group of cells from which a mother cell develops

beta_cell.definition: a cell that produces insulin in the isles of Langerhans in the pancreas

blastema.definition: a mass of undifferentiated cells from which an organ or body part develops

blastomere.definition: any cell resulting from cleavage of a fertilized egg

daughter_cell.definition: a cell formed by the division or budding of another cell

ameloblast.definition: a cell from which tooth enamel develops

erythroblast.definition: a nucleated cell in bone marrow from which red blood cells develop

sideroblast.definition: an erythroblast having granules of ferritin

fibroblast.definition: a cell from which connective tissue develops

neuroblast.definition: a cell from which a nerve cell develops

osteoblast.definition: a cell from which bone develops

fiber (cell).definition: any of several elongated, threadlike cells (especially a muscle fiber or a nerve fiber)

nerve_fiber.definition: a threadlike extension of a nerve cell

axon.definition: long nerve fiber that conducts away from the cell body of the neuron

dendrite.definition: short fiber that conducts toward the cell body of the neuron

effector.definition: a nerve fiber that terminates on a muscle or gland and stimulates contraction or secretion

medullated_nerve_fiber.definition: a nerve fiber encased in a sheath of myelin

motor_fiber.definition: a nerve fiber that carries impulses toward the muscles or glands

sensory_fiber.definition: a nerve fiber that carries impulses toward the central nervous system

flagellated_cell.definition: any cell or one-celled organism equipped with a flagellum

choanocyte.definition: any of the flagellated cells in sponges having a collar of cytoplasm around the flagellum; they maintain a flow of water through the body

gametocyte.definition: an immature animal or plant cell that develops into a gamete by meiosis

oocyte.definition: a female gametocyte that develops into an ovum after two meiotic divisions

spermatocyte.definition: a male gametocyte that develops into four spermatids

kupffer's_cell.definition: specialized cells in the liver that destroy bacteria, foreign proteins, and worn-out blood cells

leydig_cell.definition: a cell in the testes that secretes the hormone testosterone

mother_cell.definition: cell from which another cell of an organism (usually of a different sort) develops

spore_mother_cell.definition: cell from which a spore develops

plant_cell.definition: a cell that is a structural and functional unit of a plant

polar_body.definition: a small cell containing little cytoplasm that is produced along with the oocyte and later discarded

reproductive_cell.definition: a spermatozoon or an ovum; a cell responsible for transmitting DNA to the next generation

gamete.definition: a mature sexual reproductive cell having a single set of unpaired chromosomes

anisogamete.definition: either of a pair of unlike gametes especially those unlike in size

antherozoid.definition: a motile male gamete of a plant such as an alga or fern or gymnosperm

isogamete.definition: either of a pair of conjugating gametes of the same size and structure

oosphere.definition: a gamete; used especially of lower plants

ovum.definition: the female reproductive cell; the female gamete

egg.definition: animal reproductive body consisting of an ovum or embryo together with nutritive and protective envelopes; especially the thin-shelled reproductive body laid by e.g. female birds

nit.definition: egg or young of an insect parasitic on mammals especially a sucking louse; often attached to a hair or item of clothing

spawn.definition: the mass of eggs deposited by fish or amphibians or molluscs

roe.definition: the egg mass or spawn of certain crustaceans such as the lobster

ootid.definition: mature ovum after penetration by sperm but before the formation of a zygote

sperm.definition: the male reproductive cell; the male gamete

spermatid.definition: an immature gamete produced by a spermatocyte; develops into a spermatozoon

sertoli_cell.definition: elongated cells found in the seminiferous tubules of the testis; apparently they nourish the spermatids

somatic_cell.definition: any of the cells of a plant or animal except the reproductive cells; a cell that does not participate in the production of gametes

muscle_cell.definition: an elongated contractile cell that forms the muscles of the body

striated_muscle_cell.definition: an elongated contractile cell in striated muscle tissue

blood_cell.definition: either of two types of cells (erythrocytes and leukocytes) and sometimes including platelets

packed_cells.definition: a preparation of blood cells separated from the liquid plasma

red_blood_cell.definition: a mature blood cell that contains hemoglobin to carry oxygen to the bodily tissues; a biconcave disc that has no nucleus

acanthocyte.definition: an abnormal red blood cell that has thorny projections of protoplasm

megaloblast.definition: abnormally large red blood cell present in pernicious anemia and folic acid deficiency

megalocyte.definition: abnormally large red blood cell (associated with pernicious anemia)

microcyte.definition: an abnormally small red blood cell (less than 5 microns in diameter)

reticulocyte.definition: an immature red blood cell containing a network of filaments or granules

sickle_cell.definition: an abnormal red blood cell that has a crescent shape and an abnormal form of hemoglobin

siderocyte.definition: an abnormal red blood cell containing granules of iron not bound in hemoglobin

spherocyte.definition: an abnormal spherical red blood cell

target_cell (red_blood_cell).definition: an abnormal red blood cell with the appearance of a dark ring surrounding a dark center; associated with anemia

bone_cell.definition: a cell that is part of a bone

megakaryocyte.definition: a large bone marrow cell; regarded as the source of blood platelets

osteoclast.definition: cell that functions in the breakdown and resorption of bone tissue

epithelial_cell.definition: one of the closely packed cells forming the epithelium

columnar_cell.definition: an epithelial cell that is shaped like a column; some have cilia

spongioblast.definition: any of various columnar epithelial cells in the central nervous system that develop into neuroglia

cuboidal_cell.definition: an epithelial cell that shaped like a cube

goblet_cell.definition: an epithelial cell that secretes mucous

hair_cell.definition: a sensory epithelial cell present in the organ of Corti

squamous_cell.definition: an epithelial cell that is flat like a plate and form a single layer of epithelial tissue

taste_cell.definition: an epithelial cell in a taste bud that activates sensory fibers of the facial nerve or the glossopharyngeal nerve or the vagus nerve

hybridoma.definition: a hybrid cell resulting from the fusion of a lymphocyte and a tumor cell; used to culture a specific monoclonal antibody

mast_cell.definition: a large connective tissue cell that contains histamine and heparin and serotonin which are released in allergic reactions or in response to injury or inflammation

neoplastic_cell.definition: a cell that is part of tumor

cancer_cell.definition: a cell that is part of a malignant tumor

nerve_cell.definition: a cell that is specialized to conduct nerve impulses

brain_cell.definition: a nerve cell in the brain

golgi's_cell.definition: a neuron in the cerebral cortex with short dendrites and with either a long axon or a short axon that ramifies in the grey matter

purkinje_cell.definition: a large densely branching neuron that is the characteristic cell of the cerebellar cortex

ganglion_cell.definition: a nerve cell whose body is outside the central nervous system

motor_neuron.definition: a neuron conducting impulses outwards from the brain or spinal cord

sensory_neuron.definition: a neuron conducting impulses inwards to the brain or spinal cord

fibrous_astrocyte.definition: star-shaped cells with long processes; found in the white matter of the brain and spinal cord

protoplasmic_astrocyte.definition: a kind of astrocyte found in the grey matter

microgliacyte.definition: a cell of the microglia that may become phagocytic and collect waste products of nerve tissue

phagocyte.definition: a cell that engulfs and digests debris and invading microorganisms

fixed_phagocyte.definition: a phagocyte that does not circulate in the blood but is fixed in the liver or spleen or bone marrow etc.

free_phagocyte.definition: a phagocyte that circulates in the blood

leukocyte.definition: blood cells that engulf and digest bacteria and fungi; an important part of the body's defense system

basophil.definition: a leukocyte with basophilic granules easily stained by basic stains

eosinophil.definition: a leukocyte readily stained with eosin

granulocyte.definition: a leukocyte that has granules in its cytoplasm

lymphocyte.definition: an agranulocytic leukocyte that normally makes up a quarter of the white blood cell count but increases in the presence of infection

b_cell.definition: a lymphocyte derived from bone marrow that provides humoral immunity; it recognizes free antigen molecules in solution and matures into plasma cells that secrete immunoglobulin (antibodies) that inactivate the antigens

plasma_cell.definition: a cell that develops from a B lymphocyte in reaction to a specific antigen; found in bone marrow and sometimes in the blood

plasmablast.definition: the precursor of a plasma cell

t_cell.definition: a small lymphocyte developed in the thymus; it orchestrates the immune system's response to infected or malignant cells

helper_t_cell.definition: T cell with CD4 receptor that recognizes antigens on the surface of a virus-infected cell and secretes lymphokines that stimulate B cells and killer T cells; helper T cells are infected and killed by the AIDS virus

killer_t_cell.definition: T cell with CD8 receptor that recognizes antigens on the surface of a virus-infected cell and binds to the infected cell and kill it

monocyte.definition: a type of granular leukocyte that functions in the ingestion of bacteria

monoblast.definition: a large immature monocyte normally found in bone marrow

myeloblast.definition: a precursor of leukocytes that normally occurs only in bone marrow

myelocyte.definition: an immature leukocyte normally found in bone marrow

neutrophil.definition: the chief phagocytic leukocyte; stains with either basic or acid dyes

microphage.definition: a neutrophil that ingests small things (as bacteria)

macrophage.definition: a large phagocyte; some are fixed and other circulate in the blood stream

histiocyte.definition: a macrophage that is found in connective tissue

schwann_cell.definition: any cell that covers the nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system and forms the myelin sheath

skin_cell.definition: any of the cells making up the skin

epidermal_cell.definition: any of the cells making up the epidermis

melanoblast.definition: an epidermal cell that is a precursor of a melanocyte

melanocyte.definition: a cell in the basal layer of the epidermis that produces melanin under the control of the melanocyte-stimulating hormone

prickle_cell.definition: a cell in the germinal layer of the skin (the prickle-cell layer); has many spines and radiating processes

stem_cell.definition: an undifferentiated cell whose daughter cells may differentiate into other cell types (such as blood cells)

hematopoeitic_stem_cell.definition: blood forming stem cells in the bone marrow; T cells and B cells arise from these stem cells

target_cell (somatic_cell).definition: any cell that has a specific receptor for an antigen or antibody or hormone or drug, or is the focus of contact by a virus or phagocyte or nerve fiber etc.

visual_cell.definition: one of the cells of the retina that is sensitive to light

cone (visual_cell).definition: a visual receptor cell in the retina that is sensitive to bright light and to color

rod (visual_cell).definition: a visual receptor cell that is sensitive to dim light

homozygote.definition: (genetics) an organism having two identical alleles of a particular gene and so breeding true for the particular characteristic

wildlife.definition: all living things (except people) that are undomesticated

organism.definition: a living thing that has (or can develop) the ability to act or function independently

recombinant.definition: a cell or organism in which genetic recombination has occurred

aerobe.definition: an organism (especially a bacterium) that requires air or free oxygen for life

amphidiploid.definition: (genetics) an organism or cell having a diploid set of chromosomes from each parent

anaerobe.definition: an organism (especially a bacterium) that does not require air or free oxygen to live

obligate_anaerobe.definition: an organism that cannot grow in the presence of oxygen

animal.definition: a living organism characterized by voluntary movement

acrodont.definition: an animal having teeth consolidated with the summit of the alveolar ridge without sockets

appendicularia.definition: free-swimming tadpole-shaped pelagic tunicate resembling larvae of other tunicates

sea_squirt.definition: ascidian that can contract its body and eject streams of water

doliolum.definition: free-swimming oceanic tunicate with a barrel-shaped transparent body

larvacean.definition: any member of the class Larvacea

salp.definition: minute floating marine tunicate having a transparent body with an opening at each end

vertebrate.definition: animals having a bony or cartilaginous skeleton with a segmented spinal column and a large brain enclosed in a skull or cranium

amniota.definition: higher vertebrates (reptiles, birds and mammals) possessing an amnion during development

leptodactylid_frog.definition: toothed frogs: terrestrial or aquatic or arboreal

midwife_toad.definition: similar in habit to Alytes obstetricians

obstetrical_toad.definition: European toad whose male carries the fertilized eggs wrapped around its hind legs until they hatch

robber_frog.definition: small terrestrial frog of tropical America

southern_spadefoot.definition: this spadefoot toad lives in the southwestern United States

western_spadefoot.definition: this spadefoot toad live in California

tailed_frog.definition: western North American frog with a taillike copulatory organ

surinam_toad.definition: a South American toad; incubates its young in pits in the skin of its back

chorus_frog.definition: any of several small North American frogs having a loud call

cricket_frog.definition: either of two frogs with a clicking call

northern_cricket_frog.definition: a cricket frog of eastern and central United States

pacific_tree_toad.definition: the most commonly heard frog on the Pacific coast of America

agua.definition: largest known toad species; native to Central America; valuable destroyer of insect pests

american_green_toad.definition: small green or yellow-green toad with small black bars and stripes

bufo.definition: any toad of the genus Bufo

texas_toad.definition: nocturnal burrowing toad of mesquite woodland and prairies of the United States southwest

western_toad.definition: of a great variety of habitats from southern Alaska to Baja California west of the Rockies

yosemite_toad.definition: of high Sierra Nevada meadows and forest borders

western_narrow-mouthed_toad.definition: small secretive toad with smooth tough skin of central and western North America

ichyostega.definition: early tetrapod amphibian found in Greenland

eft.definition: a newt in its terrestrial stage of development

california_newt.definition: newt that is similar to Taricha granulosa in characteristics and habitat

red_eft.definition: red terrestrial form of a common North American newt

olympic_salamander.definition: small large-eyed semiaquatic salamander of the United States Northwest

pacific_giant_salamander.definition: large (to 7 inches) salamander of western North America

shasta_salamander.definition: primarily a cave dweller in the Mount Shasta area

western_red-backed_salamander.definition: salamander of the Pacific coast of North America

fish.definition: any of various mostly cold-blooded aquatic vertebrates usually having scales and breathing through gills

bony_fish.definition: any fish of the class Osteichthyes

crossopterygian.definition: any fish of the order Crossopterygii; most known only in fossil form

coelacanth.definition: fish thought to have been extinct since the Cretaceous period but found in 1938 off the coast of Africa

teleost_fish.definition: a bony fish of the subclass Teleostei

biplane_flying_fish.definition: having both pectoral and pelvic fins enlarged

ganoid.definition: primitive fishes having thick bony scales with a shiny covering

chinese_paddlefish.definition: fish of larger rivers of China similar to the Mississippi paddlefish

gar.definition: primitive predaceous North American fish covered with hard scales and having long jaws with needlelike teeth

beluga.definition: valuable source of caviar and isinglass; found in Black and Caspian seas

pacific_sturgeon.definition: food and game fish of marine and fresh waters of northwestern coast of North America

halfbeak.definition: tropical and subtropical marine and freshwater fishes having an elongated body and long protruding lower jaw

timucu.definition: found in warm waters of western Atlantic

deepwater_pipefish.definition: a fish 8 inches long; found from eastern Florida to western Caribbean

saury.definition: slender long-beaked fish of temperate Atlantic waters

soft-finned_fish.definition: any fish of the superorder Malacopterygii

mediterranean_anchovy.definition: esteemed for its flavor; usually preserved or used for sauces and relishes

argentine.definition: any of various small silver-scaled salmon-like marine fishes

beaked_salmon.definition: fish of sandy areas of western Pacific and Indian oceans having an angular snout for burrowing into sand

bonefish.definition: slender silvery marine fish found in tropical mud flats and mangrove lagoons

armored_catfish.definition: South American catfish having the body covered with bony plates

bullhead (catfish).definition: any of several common freshwater catfishes of the United States

brown_bullhead.definition: freshwater catfish of eastern United States

horned_pout.definition: catfish common in eastern United States

channel_catfish.definition: freshwater food fish common throughout central United States

blue_catfish.definition: a large catfish of the Mississippi valley

flathead_catfish.definition: large catfish of central United States having a flattened head and projecting jaw

sea_catfish.definition: any of numerous marine fishes most of which are mouthbreeders; not used for food

crucifix_fish.definition: sea catfish of the Caribbean area

european_catfish.definition: large elongated catfish of central and eastern Europe

pacific_sardine.definition: small pilchards common off the pacific coast of North America

catostomid.definition: a cypriniform fish of the family Catostomidae

buffalo_fish.definition: any of several large suckers of the Mississippi valley

hog_sucker.definition: widely distributed in warm clear shallow streams

redhorse.definition: North American sucker with reddish fins

characin.definition: any freshwater fish of the family Characinidae

cardinal_tetra.definition: small bright red and blue aquarium fish from streams in Brazil and Colombia

piranha.definition: small voraciously carnivorous freshwater fishes of South America that attack and destroy living animals

crucian_carp.definition: European carp closely resembling wild goldfish

dace.definition: small European freshwater fish with a slender bluish-green body

goldfish.definition: small golden or orange-red freshwater fishes of Eurasia used as pond or aquarium fishes

eagle_ray.definition: powerful free-swimming tropical ray noted for `soaring' by flapping winglike fins; usually harmless but has venomous tissue near base of the tail as in stingrays

cownose_ray.definition: large ray found along eastern coast of North America

spotted_eagle_ray.definition: ray with back covered with white or yellow spots; widely distributed in warm seas

electric_ray.definition: any sluggish bottom-dwelling ray of the order Torpediniformes having a rounded body and electric organs on each side of the head capable of emitting strong electric discharges

guitarfish.definition: primitive tropical bottom-dwelling ray with a guitar-shaped body

manta (ray).definition: extremely large pelagic tropical ray that feeds on plankton and small fishes; usually harmless but its size make it dangerous if harpooned

atlantic_manta.definition: largest manta (to 22 feet across wings); found worldwide but common in Gulf of Mexico and along southern coasts of United States; primarily oceanic

devil_ray.definition: small manta (to 4 feet) that travels in schools

sawfish.definition: primitive ray with sharp teeth on each edge of a long flattened snout

smalltooth_sawfish.definition: commonly found in tropical bays and estuaries; not aggressive

skate (ray).definition: large edible rays having a long snout and thick tail with pectoral fins continuous with the head; swim by undulating the edges of the pectoral fins

barndoor_skate.definition: one of the largest skates (to 5 feet); an active skate easy to hook

grey_skate.definition: common European skate used as food

little_skate.definition: most plentiful skate in North American inshore waters in summer; to 21 inches

thorny_skate.definition: cold-water bottom fish with spines on the back; to 40 inches

stingray.definition: large venomous ray with large barbed spines near the base of a thin whiplike tail capable of inflicting severe wounds

butterfly_ray.definition: a stingray with a short tail and a broad fin

roughtail_stingray.definition: one of the largest stingrays; found from Cape Cod to Cape Hatteras

shark (elasmobranch).definition: any of numerous elongate mostly marine carnivorous fishes with heterocercal caudal fins and tough skin covered with small toothlike scales

angel_shark.definition: sharks with broad flat bodies and winglike pectoral fins but that swim the way sharks do

carpet_shark.definition: shark of the western Pacific with flattened body and mottled skin

cat_shark.definition: small bottom-dwelling sharks with cat-like eyes; found along continental slopes

cow_shark.definition: large primitive shark widely distributed in warm seas

smooth_dogfish.definition: small bottom-dwelling shark found along both Atlantic coasts

american_smooth_dogfish.definition: found along the Atlantic coast of the Americas

florida_smoothhound.definition: found from the northern Gulf of Mexico to Brazil

smoothhound.definition: smooth dogfish of European coastal waters

whitetip_shark (smooth_dogfish).definition: smooth dogfish of Pacific and Indian Oceans and Red Sea having white-tipped dorsal and caudal fins

atlantic_spiny_dogfish.definition: destructive dogfish of the Atlantic coastal waters of America and Europe; widely used in anatomy classes

pacific_spiny_dogfish.definition: dogfish of Pacific coast of North America

shovelhead.definition: small harmless hammerhead having a spade-shaped head; abundant in bays and estuaries

smalleye_hammerhead.definition: fished for the hide and vitamin-rich liver

smooth_hammerhead.definition: fished for the hides and vitamin-rich liver

basking_shark.definition: large harmless plankton-eating northern shark; often swims slowly or floats at the sea surface

great_white_shark.definition: large aggressive shark widespread in warm seas; known to attack humans

mako.definition: powerful mackerel shark of the Atlantic and Pacific

bonito_shark.definition: common blue-grey shark of southwest Pacific; sport and food fish

longfin_mako.definition: similar to shortfin mako but darker blue

shortfin_mako.definition: very swift active bluish shark found worldwide in warm waters; important game fish

porbeagle.definition: voracious pointed-nose shark of northern Atlantic and Pacific

nurse_shark.definition: small bottom-dwelling shark of warm shallow waters on both coasts of North America and South America and from southeast Asia to Australia

requiem_shark.definition: any of numerous sharks from small relatively harmless bottom-dwellers to large dangerous oceanic and coastal species

blacktip_shark.definition: widely distributed shallow-water shark with fins seemingly dipped in ink

blue_shark.definition: slender cosmopolitan, pelagic shark; blue body shades to white belly; dangerous especially during maritime disasters

bull_shark.definition: a most common shark in temperate and tropical coastal waters worldwide; heavy-bodied and dangerous

dusky_shark.definition: relatively slender blue-grey shark; nearly worldwide in tropical and temperate waters

lemon_shark.definition: common shallow-water schooling shark of the Atlantic from North Carolina to Brazil and off west Africa; dangerous

sandbar_shark.definition: most common grey shark along coasts of middle Atlantic states; sluggish and occasionally caught by fishermen

soupfin_shark.definition: Pacific shark valued for its fins (used by Chinese in soup) and liver (rich in vitamin A)

tiger_shark.definition: large dangerous warm-water shark with striped or spotted body

whitetip_shark (requiem_shark).definition: large deep-water shark with white-tipped dorsal fin; worldwide distribution; most dangerous shark

sand_tiger.definition: shallow-water shark with sharp jagged teeth found on both sides of Atlantic; sometimes dangerous to swimmers

whale_shark.definition: large spotted shark of warm surface waters worldwide; resembles a whale and feeds chiefly on plankton

holocephalan.definition: fish with high compressed head and a body tapering off into a long tail

chimaera.definition: a deep-sea fish with a tapering body, smooth skin, and long threadlike tail

food_fish.definition: any fish used for food by human beings

pacific_herring.definition: important food fish of the northern Pacific

sardine.definition: any of various small edible herring or related food fishes frequently canned

brisling.definition: small herring processed like a sardine

sild.definition: any of various young herrings (other than brislings) canned as sardines in Norway

common_american_shad.definition: shad of Atlantic coast of North America; naturalized to Pacific coast

river_shad.definition: shad that spawns in streams of the Mississippi drainage; very similar to Alosa sapidissima

coho.definition: small salmon of northern Pacific coasts and the Great Lakes

trout.definition: any of various game and food fishes of cool fresh waters mostly smaller than typical salmons

brook_trout.definition: North American freshwater trout; introduced in Europe

brown_trout.definition: speckled trout of European rivers; introduced in North America

sea_trout (brown_trout).definition: silvery marine variety of brown trout that migrates to fresh water to spawn

lake_trout.definition: large fork-tailed trout of lakes of Canada and the northern United States

rainbow_trout.definition: found in Pacific coastal waters and streams from lower California to Alaska

lake_whitefish.definition: found in the Great Lakes and north to Alaska

rocky_mountain_whitefish.definition: whitefish of the western United States and Canada

round_whitefish.definition: a whitefish with a bronze back; of northern North America and Siberia

hogchoker.definition: useless as food; in coastal streams from Maine to Texas and Panama

sand_sole.definition: a common flatfish of the Pacific coast of North America

belted_sandfish.definition: found in warm shallow waters of western Atlantic

black_sea_bass.definition: bluish black-striped sea bass of the Atlantic coast of the United States

blackmouth_bass.definition: small marine fish with black mouth and gill cavity

grouper.definition: usually solitary bottom sea basses of warm seas

grey_snapper.definition: found in shallow waters off the coast of Florida

mutton_snapper.definition: similar to and often marketed as `red snapper'

red_snapper.definition: an esteemed food fish with pinkish red head and body; common in the Atlantic coastal waters of North America and the Gulf of Mexico

barracouta.definition: a large marine food fish common on the coasts of Australia, New Zealand, and southern Africa

game_fish.definition: any fish providing sport for the angler

mouthbreeder.definition: any of various fishes that carry their eggs and their young in their mouths

thornbill.definition: any of various South American hummingbirds with a sharp pointed bill

little_auk.definition: small short-billed auk abundant in Arctic regions

larid.definition: long-winged web-footed aquatic bird of the gull family

black-footed_albatross.definition: a variety of albatross with black feet

wandering_albatross.definition: very large albatross; white with wide black wings

giant_petrel.definition: large brownish petrel chiefly of Antarctic seas

manx_shearwater.definition: small black-and-white shearwater common in the northeastern Atlantic

striped_button_quail.definition: a variety of button quail having stripes

crested_cariama.definition: Brazilian Cariama; sole representative of the genus Cariama

heron.definition: grey or white wading bird with long neck and long legs and (usually) long bill

boatbill.definition: tropical American heron related to night herons

egret.definition: any of various usually white herons having long plumes during breeding season

great_white_heron (egret).definition: widely distributed Old World white egret

great_blue_heron.definition: large American heron having bluish-grey plumage

great_white_heron (heron).definition: large white heron of Florida and the Florida Keys

little_blue_heron.definition: small bluish-grey heron of the western hemisphere

wood_ibis (ibis).definition: any of several Old World birds of the genus Ibis

limpkin.definition: wading bird of Florida, Cuba and Jamaica having a drooping bill and a distinctive wailing call

ortygan.definition: any of several East Indian birds

plain_wanderer.definition: small Australian bird related to the button quail; classified as wading bird but inhabits plains

coot.definition: slate-black slow-flying birds somewhat resembling ducks

american_coot.definition: a coot found in North America

crake.definition: any of several short-billed Old World rails

corncrake.definition: common Eurasian rail that frequents grain fields

spotted_crake.definition: Eurasian rail of swamps and marshes

notornis.definition: flightless New Zealand birds similar to gallinules

weka.definition: flightless New Zealand rail of thievish disposition having short wings each with a spur used in fighting

shoebill.definition: large stork-like bird of the valley of the White Nile with a broad bill suggesting a wooden shoe

avocet.definition: long-legged web-footed black-and-white shorebird with slender upward-curving bill

lapwing.definition: large crested Old World plover having wattles and spurs

redshank.definition: a common Old World wading bird with long red legs

tattler.definition: any of several long-legged shorebirds having a loud whistling cry

willet.definition: large North American shorebird of eastern and Gulf Coasts

yellowlegs.definition: either of two North American shorebird with yellow legs

great_snipe.definition: Old World snipe larger and darker than the whole snipe

jacksnipe.definition: a small short-billed Old World snipe

whole_snipe.definition: common snipe of Eurasia and Africa

banded_stilt.definition: web-footed Australian stilt with reddish-brown pectoral markings

stone_curlew.definition: large-headed large-eyed crepuscular or nocturnal shorebird of the Old World and tropical America having a thickened knee joint

surfbird.definition: sandpiper-like shorebird of Pacific coasts of North America and South America

bristletail.definition: small wingless insect with a long bristlelike tail

firebrat.definition: lives in warm moist areas e.g. around furnaces

jumping_bristletail.definition: wingless insect living in dark moist places as under dead tree trunks; they make erratic leaps when disturbed

silverfish (thysanuran_insect).definition: silver-grey wingless insect found in houses feeding on book bindings and starched clothing

caddis_fly.definition: small moth-like insect having two pairs of hairy membranous wings and aquatic larvae

web_spinner.definition: any of a small order of slender typically tropical insects that nest in colonies in silken tunnels that they spin

worker (insect).definition: sterile member of a colony of social insects that forages for food and cares for the larvae

soldier (worker).definition: a wingless sterile ant or termite having a large head and powerful jaws adapted for defending the colony

worker_bee.definition: sterile bee specialized to collect food and maintain the hive

instar.definition: an insect or other arthropod between molts

merostomata.definition: used in some classifications; includes the orders Xiphosura and Eurypterida

millipede.definition: any of numerous herbivorous nonpoisonous arthropods having a cylindrical body of 20 to 100 or more segments most with two pairs of legs

myriapod.definition: general term for any terrestrial arthropod having an elongated body composed of many similar segments: e.g. centipedes and millipedes

onychophoran.definition: any of numerous velvety-skinned wormlike carnivorous animals common in tropical forests having characteristics of both arthropods and annelid worms

sea_spider.definition: any of various small spiderlike marine arthropods having small thin bodies and long slender legs

tardigrade.definition: an arthropod of the division Tardigrada

tongue_worm.definition: wormlike arthropod having two pairs of hooks at the sides of the mouth; parasitic in nasal sinuses of mammals

trilobite.definition: an extinct arthropod that was abundant in Paleozoic times; had an exoskeleton divided into three parts

brachiopod.definition: marine animal with bivalve shell having a pair of arms bearing tentacles for capturing food; found worldwide

bryozoan.definition: sessile aquatic animal forming mossy colonies of small polyps each having a curved or circular ridge bearing tentacles; attach to stones or seaweed and reproduce by budding

coelenterate.definition: radially symmetrical animals having saclike bodies with only one opening and tentacles with stinging structures; they occur in polyp and medusa forms

anthozoan.definition: sessile marine coelenterates including solitary and colonial polyps; the medusoid phase is entirely suppressed

coral.definition: marine colonial polyp characterized by a calcareous skeleton; masses in a variety of shapes often forming reefs

gorgonian.definition: corals having a horny or calcareous branching skeleton

red_coral.definition: corals of especially the Mediterranean having pink or red color used for ornaments and jewelry

sea_fan.definition: corals having a treelike or fan-shaped horny skeleton

stony_coral.definition: corals having calcareous skeletons aggregations of which form reefs and islands

brain_coral.definition: massive reef-building coral having a convoluted and furrowed surface

mushroom_coral.definition: flattened disk-shaped stony coral (usually solitary and unattached)

sea_anemone.definition: marine polyps that resemble flowers but have oral rings of tentacles; differ from corals in forming no hard skeleton

actinia.definition: any sea anemone or related animal

hydrozoan.definition: colonial coelenterates having the polyp phase dominant

hydra.definition: small tubular solitary freshwater hydrozoan polyp

planula.definition: the flat ciliated free-swimming larva of hydrozoan coelenterates

sertularian.definition: feathery colony of long-branched stems bearing stalkless paired polyps

siphonophore.definition: a floating or swimming oceanic colony of polyps often transparent or showily colored

apolemia.definition: large siphonophore of up to 50 ft long

nanomia.definition: small creatures resembling pieces of fuzzy rope; each with a cluster of swimming bells serving as the head and long elastic tentacles for drawing in prey

portuguese_man-of-war.definition: large siphonophore having a bladderlike float and stinging tentacles

praya.definition: colonial siphonophore of up to 130 ft long

jellyfish.definition: any of numerous usually marine and free-swimming coelenterates that constitute the sexually reproductive forms of hydrozoans and scyphozoans

medusa.definition: one of two forms that coelenterates take: it is the free-swimming sexual phase in the life cycle of a coelenterate; in this phase it has a gelatinous umbrella-shaped body and tentacles

polyp.definition: one of two forms that coelenterates take (e.g. a hydra or coral): usually sedentary with a hollow cylindrical body usually with a ring of tentacles around the mouth

scyphozoan.definition: any of various usually free-swimming marine coelenterates having a gelatinous medusoid stage as the dominant phase of its life cycle

ctenophore.definition: biradially symmetrical hermaphroditic solitary marine animals resembling jellyfishes having for locomotion eight rows of cilia arranged like teeth in a comb

platyctenean.definition: ctenophore have long tentacles and flattened body

sea_gooseberry.definition: ctenophore having a rounded body with longitudinal rows of cilia

venus's_girdle.definition: ctenophore having a ribbon-shaped iridescent gelatinous body

echinoderm.definition: marine invertebrates with tube feet and five-part radially symmetrical bodies

basket_star.definition: any starfish-like animal of the genera Euryale or Astrophyton or Gorgonocephalus having slender complexly branched interlacing arms radiating from a central disc

brittle_star.definition: an animal resembling a starfish with fragile whiplike arms radiating from a small central disc

crinoid.definition: primitive echinoderms having five or more feathery arms radiating from a central disk

feather_star.definition: free-swimming stalkless crinoid with ten feathery arms; found on muddy sea bottoms

sea_lily.definition: crinoid with delicate radiating arms and a stalked body attached to a hard surface

sea_cucumber.definition: echinoderm having a flexible sausage-shaped body, tentacles surrounding the mouth and tube feet; free-living mud feeders

trepang.definition: of warm coasts from Australia to Asia; used as food especially by Chinese

sea_urchin.definition: shallow-water echinoderms having soft bodies enclosed in thin spiny globular shells

edible_sea_urchin.definition: a sea urchin that can be eaten

heart_urchin.definition: sea urchin having a heart-shaped body in a rigid spiny shell

sand_dollar.definition: flattened disklike sea urchins that live on sandy bottoms

starfish.definition: echinoderms characterized by five arms extending from a central disk

ectoproct.definition: sessile mossy aquatic animal having the anus of the polyp outside the crown of tentacles

entoproct.definition: any of various moss-like aquatic animals usually forming branching colonies; each polyp having a both mouth and anus within a closed ring of tentacles

mollusk.definition: invertebrate having a soft unsegmented body usually enclosed in a shell

bivalve.definition: marine or freshwater mollusks having a soft body with platelike gills enclosed within two shells hinged together

ark_shell.definition: marine bivalve mollusk having a heavy toothed shell with a deep boat-like inner surface

clam.definition: burrowing marine mollusk living on sand or mud; the shell closes with viselike firmness

geoduck.definition: a large edible clam found burrowing deeply in sandy mud along the Pacific coast of North America; weighs up to six pounds; has siphons that can extend to several feet and cannot be withdrawn into the shell

giant_clam.definition: a large clam inhabiting reefs in the southern Pacific and weighing up to 500 pounds

quahog.definition: an edible American clam; the heavy shells were used as money by some American Indians

razor_clam.definition: marine clam having a long narrow curved thin shell

shipworm.definition: wormlike marine bivalve that bores into wooden piers and ships by means of drill-like shells

giant_northwest_shipworm.definition: giant shipworm of the Pacific coast of North America

soft-shell_clam.definition: an edible clam with thin oval-shaped shell found in coastal regions of the United States and Europe

cockle.definition: common edible, burrowing European bivalve mollusk that has a strong, rounded shell with radiating ribs

mussel.definition: marine or freshwater bivalve mollusk that lives attached to rocks etc.

freshwater_mussel.definition: bivalve mollusk abundant in rivers of central United States

pearly-shelled_mussel.definition: the pearly lining of the dark shells is a source of mother-of-pearl

thin-shelled_mussel.definition: mussel with thin fragile shells having only rudimentary hinge teeth

zebra_mussel.definition: inch long mollusk imported accidentally from Europe; clogs utility inlet pipes and feeds on edible freshwater mussels

marine_mussel.definition: marine bivalve mollusk having a dark elongated shell; live attached to solid objects especially in intertidal zones

edible_mussel.definition: a mussel with a dark shell that lives attached to rocks

oyster.definition: marine mollusks having a rough irregular shell; found on the sea bed mostly in coastal waters

bluepoint.definition: small edible oyster typically from the southern shore of Long Island

japanese_oyster.definition: a large oyster native to Japan and introduced along the Pacific coast of the United States; a candidate for introduction in Chesapeake Bay

pearl_oyster.definition: tropical marine bivalve found chiefly off eastern Asia and Pacific coast of North America and Central America; a major source of pearls

saddle_oyster.definition: thin-shelled bivalve having the right valve deeply notched

seed_oyster.definition: a young oyster especially of a size for transplantation

virginia_oyster.definition: common edible oyster of Atlantic coast of North America

window_oyster.definition: marine bivalve common in Philippine coastal waters characterized by a large thin flat translucent shell

piddock.definition: marine bivalve that bores into rock or clay or wood by means of saw-like shells

scallop.definition: edible marine bivalve having a fluted fan-shaped shell that swim by expelling water from the shell in a series of snapping motions

bay_scallop.definition: a small scallop inhabiting shallow waters and mud flats of the Atlantic coast of North America

sea_scallop.definition: a large scallop inhabiting deep waters of the Atlantic coast of North America

cephalopod.definition: marine mollusk characterized by well-developed head and eyes and sucker-bearing tentacles

chambered_nautilus.definition: cephalopod of the Indian and Pacific oceans having a spiral shell with pale pearly partitions

decapod.definition: cephalopods having eight short tentacles plus two long ones

cuttlefish.definition: ten-armed oval-bodied cephalopod with narrow fins as long as the body and a large calcareous internal shell

spirula.definition: a small tropical cephalopod of the genus Spirula having prominent eyes and short arms and a many-chambered shell coiled in a flat spiral

squid.definition: widely distributed fast-moving ten-armed cephalopod mollusk having a long tapered body with triangular tail fins

architeuthis.definition: largest mollusk known about but never seen (to 60 feet long)

ommastrephes.definition: extremely active cylindrical squid with short strong arms and large rhombic terminal fins

octopod.definition: a cephalopod with eight arms but lacking an internal shell

octopus.definition: bottom-living cephalopod having a soft oval body with eight long tentacles

paper_nautilus.definition: cephalopod mollusk of warm seas whose females have delicate papery spiral shells

chiton (mollusk).definition: primitive elongated bilaterally symmetrical marine mollusk having a mantle covered with eight calcareous plates

gastropod.definition: a class of mollusks typically having a one-piece coiled shell and flattened muscular foot with a head bearing stalked eyes

abalone.definition: any of various large edible marine gastropods of the genus Haliotis having an ear-shaped shell with pearly interior

ormer.definition: an abalone found near the Channel Islands

bubble_shell.definition: marine gastropod mollusk having a very small thin shell

conch.definition: any of various edible tropical marine gastropods of the genus Strombus having a brightly-colored spiral shell with large outer lip

cowrie.definition: any of numerous tropical marine gastropods of the genus Cypraea having highly polished usually brightly marked shells

money_cowrie.definition: cowrie whose shell is used for money in parts of the southern Pacific and in parts of Africa

tiger_cowrie.definition: cowrie whose shell is used for ornament

physa.definition: any member of the genus Physa

river_limpet.definition: minute conical gastropod superficially resembling a limpet but living and feeding on freshwater plants

sea_hare.definition: naked marine gastropod having a soft body with reduced internal shell and two pairs of ear-like tentacles

sea_slug.definition: any of various marine gastropods of the suborder Nudibranchia having a shell-less and often beautifully colored body

seasnail.definition: any of several creeping marine gastropods with a spirally coiled shell: whelks; tritons; moon shells; neritids

limpet.definition: any of various usually marine gastropods with low conical shells; found clinging to rocks in littoral areas

keyhole_limpet.definition: marine limpet having a conical shell with an opening at the apex

moon_shell.definition: marine gastropods having smooth rounded shells that form short spires

neritid.definition: operculate seasnail of coastal waters with a short spiral shell

bleeding_tooth.definition: gastropod having reddish toothlike projections around the shell opening; of the Caribbean area

nerita.definition: a neritid gastropod having a short smooth or spirally ridged shell with thick usually toothed outer lip and toothed operculum

neritina.definition: ornately marked and brightly colored snails of brackish waters

triton.definition: tropical marine gastropods having beautifully colored spiral shells

whelk.definition: large carnivorous marine gastropods of coastal waters and intertidal regions having a strong snail-like shell

slug.definition: any of various terrestrial gastropods having an elongated slimy body and no external shell

snail.definition: freshwater or marine or terrestrial gastropod mollusk usually having an external enclosing spiral shell

edible_snail.definition: one of the chief edible snails

garden_snail.definition: any of several inedible snails of the genus Helix; often destructive pests

brown_snail.definition: serious garden pest having a brown shell with paler zigzag markings; nearly cosmopolitan in distribution

scorpion_shell.definition: any of numerous tropical marine snails that as adults have the outer lip of the aperture produced into a series of long curved spines

solenogaster.definition: deep-water wormlike mollusks lacking calcareous plates on the body but having fine slimy spicules on the covering mantle

tooth_shell.definition: any of various seashore mollusks having a tapering tubular shell open at each end and a foot pointed like a spade for burrowing

peanut_worm.definition: small unsegmented marine worm that when disturbed retracts its anterior portion into the body giving the appearance of a peanut

phoronid.definition: hermaphrodite wormlike animal living in mud of the sea bottom

rotifer.definition: minute aquatic multicellular organisms having a ciliated wheel-like organ for feeding and locomotion; constituents of freshwater plankton

sponge.definition: primitive multicellular marine animal whose porous body is supported by a fibrous skeletal framework; usually occurs in sessile colonies

glass_sponge.definition: a siliceous sponge (with glassy spicules) of the class Hyalospongiae

venus's_flower_basket.definition: a deep-water marine sponge having a cylindrical skeleton of intricate glassy latticework; found in the waters of the East Indies and the eastern coast of Asia

symbion_pandora.definition: only known species of Cycliophora; lives symbiotically attached to a lobster's lip by an adhesive disk and feeding by means of a hairy mouth ring; its complex life cycle includes asexual and sexual phases

woodborer.definition: any of various insects or larvae or mollusks that bore into wood

worm (invertebrate).definition: any of numerous relatively small elongated soft-bodied animals especially of the phyla Annelida and Chaetognatha and Nematoda and Nemertea and Platyhelminthes; also many insect larvae

acanthocephalan.definition: any of various worms living parasitically in intestines of vertebrates having a retractile proboscis covered with many hooked spines

annelid.definition: worms with cylindrical bodies segmented both internally and externally

archiannelid.definition: small primitive marine worm lacking external segmentation and resembling polychaete larvae

leech (annelid).definition: carnivorous or bloodsucking aquatic or terrestrial worms typically having a sucker at each end

horseleech.definition: any of several large freshwater leeches

medicinal_leech.definition: large European freshwater leech formerly used for bloodletting

oligochaete.definition: hermaphroditic terrestrial and aquatic annelids having bristles borne singly along the length of the body

earthworm.definition: terrestrial worm that burrows into and helps aerate soil; often surfaces when the ground is cool or wet; used as bait by anglers

polychaete.definition: chiefly marine annelids possessing both sexes and having paired appendages (parapodia) bearing bristles

bloodworm.definition: a segmented marine worm with bright red body; often used for bait

lugworm.definition: marine worms having a row of tufted gills along each side of the back; often used for fishing bait

sea_mouse.definition: any of several large worms having a broad flattened body with a mat of coarse hairs covering the back

arrowworm.definition: any worm of the Chaetognatha; transparent marine worm with horizontal lateral and caudal fins and a row of movable curved spines at each side of the mouth

sagitta.definition: any arrowworm of the genus Sagitta

beard_worm.definition: slender animal with tentacles and a tubelike outer covering; lives on the deep ocean bottom

flatworm.definition: parasitic or free-living worms having a flattened body

fluke (flatworm).definition: parasitic flatworms having external suckers for attaching to a host

fasciolopsis_buski.definition: fluke that is parasitic on humans and swine; common in eastern Asia

liver_fluke.definition: flatworm parasitic in liver and bile ducts of domestic animals and humans

schistosome.definition: flatworms parasitic in the blood vessels of mammals

planarian.definition: free-swimming mostly freshwater flatworms; popular in laboratory studies for the ability to regenerate lost parts

tapeworm.definition: ribbonlike flatworms that are parasitic in the intestines of humans and other vertebrates

echinococcus.definition: tapeworms whose larvae are parasitic in humans and domestic animals

taenia (tapeworm).definition: tapeworms parasitic in humans which uses the pig as its intermediate host

helminth.definition: worm that is parasitic on the intestines of vertebrates especially roundworms and tapeworms and flukes

nematode.definition: unsegmented worms with elongated rounded body pointed at both ends; mostly free-living but some are parasitic

common_roundworm.definition: intestinal parasite of humans and pigs

eelworm.definition: any of various small free-living plant-parasitic roundworms

vinegar_eel.definition: minute eelworm that feeds on organisms that cause fermentation in e.g. vinegar

filaria.definition: slender threadlike roundworms living in the blood and tissues of vertebrates; transmitted as larvae by biting insects

guinea_worm.definition: parasitic roundworm of India and Africa that lives in the abdomen or beneath the skin of humans and other vertebrates

hookworm.definition: parasitic bloodsucking roundworms having hooked mouth parts to fasten to the intestinal wall of human and other hosts

pinworm.definition: small threadlike worm infesting human intestines and rectum especially in children

trichina.definition: parasitic nematode occurring in the intestines of pigs and rats and human beings and producing larvae that form cysts in skeletal muscles

ribbon_worm.definition: soft unsegmented marine worms that have a threadlike proboscis and the ability to stretch and contract

zoophyte.definition: any of various invertebrate animals resembling a plant such as a sea anemone or coral or sponge

larva.definition: the immature free-living form of most invertebrates and amphibians and fish which at hatching from the egg is fundamentally unlike its parent and must metamorphose

ascidian_tadpole.definition: free-swimming larva of ascidians; they have a tail like a tadpole that contains the notochord

bladder_worm.definition: encysted saclike larva of the tapeworm

bot.definition: botfly larva; typically develops inside the body of a horse or sheep or human

caseworm.definition: insect larva that constructs a protective case around its body

caddisworm.definition: larva of the caddis fly; constructs a case of silk covered with sand or plant debris

caterpillar (larva).definition: a wormlike and often brightly colored and hairy or spiny larva of a butterfly or moth

armyworm (caterpillar).definition: noctuid moth larvae that travel in multitudes destroying especially grass and grain

beet_armyworm.definition: moth larva that eats foliage of beets and other vegetables

bollworm.definition: any of various moth caterpillars that destroy cotton bolls

corn_earworm.definition: larva of a noctuid moth; highly destructive to especially corn and cotton and tomato crops

pink_bollworm.definition: larvae of a gelechiid moth introduced from Asia; feeds on the seeds of cotton bolls

cabbageworm.definition: toxic green larva of a cabbage butterfly

cankerworm.definition: green caterpillar of a geometrid moth; pest of various fruit and shade trees

fall_cankerworm.definition: green or brown white-striped looper; larva of Alsophila pometaria

spring_cankerworm.definition: variably colored looper; larva of Paleacrita vernata

corn_borer (caterpillar).definition: larva of the European corn borer moth; a serious pest of maize

cutworm.definition: North American moth whose larvae feed on young plant stems cutting them off at the ground

army_cutworm.definition: larvae (of a noctuid moth) that travel in large groups and destroy grains and alfalfa in the midwestern states

fall_armyworm.definition: larva of a migratory American noctuid moth; destroys grasses and small grains

measuring_worm.definition: small hairless caterpillar having legs on only its front and rear segments; mostly larvae of moths of the family Geometridae

potato_tuberworm.definition: larva of potato moth; mines in leaves and stems of e.g. potatoes and tobacco

ailanthus_silkworm.definition: large green silkworm of the cynthia moth

tent_caterpillar.definition: the larvae of moths that build and live in communal silken webs in orchard and shade trees

forest_tent_caterpillar.definition: larvae of a gregarious North American moth that spins a web resembling a carpet rather than a tent; serious defoliator of deciduous trees

tobacco_hornworm.definition: large green white-striped hawkmoth larva that feeds on tobacco and related plants; similar to tomato hornworm

tomato_hornworm.definition: large green white-striped hawkmoth larva that feeds on tomato and potato plants; similar to tobacco hornworm

webworm.definition: several gregarious moth larvae that spin webs over foliage on which they feed

woolly_bear.definition: caterpillar of numerous moths characterized by a dense coat of woolly hairs; feed on plants and some are destructive pests

woolly_bear_moth.definition: larva of moth of the family Arctiidae

cercaria.definition: tadpole-shaped parasitic larva of a trematode worm; tail disappears in adult stage

doodlebug (larva).definition: the larva of any of several insects

grub.definition: a soft thick wormlike larva of certain beetles and other insects

leatherjacket (grub).definition: tough-skinned larva of certain crane flies

maggot.definition: the larva of the housefly and blowfly commonly found in decaying organic matter

hellgrammiate.definition: large brown aquatic larva of the dobsonfly; used as fishing bait

leptocephalus.definition: slender transparent larva of eels and certain fishes

mealworm.definition: the larva of beetles of the family Tenebrionidae

nymph (larva).definition: a larva of an insect with incomplete metamorphosis (as the dragonfly or mayfly)

strawworm.definition: larva of chalcid flies injurious to the straw of wheat and other grains

wireworm.definition: wormlike larva of various elaterid beetles; feeds on roots of many crop plants

male (animal).definition: an animal that produces gametes (spermatozoa) that can fertilize female gametes (ova)

male_horse.definition: the male of species Equus caballus

stud (stallion).definition: adult male horse kept for breeding

sire (male).definition: male parent of an animal especially a domestic animal such as a horse

marine_animal.definition: any of numerous animals inhabiting the sea including e.g. fishes and molluscs and many mammals

by-catch.definition: unwanted marine creatures that are caught in the nets while fishing for another species

mate (animal).definition: the partner of an animal (especially a sexual partner)

metazoan.definition: any animal of the subkingdom Metazoa; all animals except protozoans and sponges

migrator.definition: an animal (especially birds and fish) that travels between different habitats at particular times of the year

molter.definition: an animal (especially birds and arthropods and reptiles) that periodically shed their outer layer (feathers or cuticle or skin or hair)

mutant (animal).definition: an animal that has undergone mutation

omnivore (animal).definition: an animal that feeds on both animal and vegetable substances

peeper.definition: an animal that makes short high-pitched sounds

pest (animal).definition: any unwanted and destructive insect or other animal that attacks food or crops or livestock etc.

vermin (pest).definition: any of various small animals or insects that are pests; e.g. cockroaches or rats

pet.definition: a domesticated animal kept for companionship or amusement

pleurodont.definition: an animal having teeth fused with the inner surface of the alveolar ridge without sockets

poikilotherm.definition: an animal whose body temperature varies with the temperature of its surroundings; any animal except birds and mammals

predator.definition: any animal that lives by preying on other animals

carnivore (predator).definition: any animal that feeds on flesh

prey (animal).definition: animal hunted or caught for food

greyhound.definition: a tall slender dog of an ancient breed noted for swiftness and keen sight; used as a racing dog

italian_greyhound.definition: a toy dog developed from the greyhound

whippet.definition: small slender dog of greyhound type developed in England

steeplechaser.definition: a horse trained to run in steeplechases

range_animal.definition: any animal that lives and grazes in the grassy open land of western North America (especially horses, cattle, sheep)

scavenger.definition: any animal that feeds on refuse and other decaying organic matter

bottom-feeder (scavenger).definition: a scavenger that feeds low on the food chain

stayer.definition: a person or other animal having powers of endurance or perseverance

stunt.definition: a creature (especially a whale) that has been prevented from attaining full growth

survivor (animal).definition: an animal that survives in spite of adversity

thoroughbred (animal).definition: a pedigreed animal of unmixed lineage; used especially of horses

varmint.definition: any usually predatory wild animal considered undesirable; e.g., coyote

work_animal.definition: an animal trained for and used for heavy labor

beast_of_burden.definition: an animal such as a donkey or ox or elephant used for transporting loads or doing other heavy work

pack_animal.definition: an animal (such as a mule or burro or horse) used to carry loads

packhorse.definition: a workhorse used as a pack animal

draft_animal.definition: an animal used for pulling heavy loads

brit (young_fish).definition: the young of a herring or sprat or similar fish

whitebait.definition: the edible young of especially herrings and sprats and smelts

orphan (young).definition: a young animal without a mother

spat (young).definition: a young oyster or other bivalve

young_bird.definition: a bird that is still young

chick.definition: young bird especially of domestic fowl

fledgling.definition: young bird that has just fledged or become capable of flying

dogie.definition: motherless calf in a range herd of cattle

maverick (calf).definition: an unbranded range animal (especially a stray calf); belongs to the first person who puts a brand on it

cub (young_mammal).definition: the young of certain carnivorous mammals such as the bear or wolf or lion

filly.definition: a young female horse under the age of four

colt (foal).definition: a young male horse under the age of four

kit (young_mammal).definition: young of any of various fur-bearing animals

baa-lamb.definition: child's word for a sheep or lamb

hog (lamb).definition: a sheep up to the age of one year; one yet to be sheared

pup.definition: young of any of various canines such as a dog or wolf

suckling.definition: a young mammal that has not been weaned

zooplankton.definition: animal constituent of plankton; mainly small crustaceans and fish larvae

animalcule.definition: microscopic organism such as an amoeba or paramecium

atavist.definition: an organism that has the characteristics of a more primitive type of that organism

benthos (organism).definition: organisms (plants and animals) that live at or near the bottom of a sea

carrier (organism).definition: (genetics) an organism that possesses a recessive gene whose effect is masked by a dominant allele; the associated trait is not apparent but can be passed on to offspring

clone.definition: a group of genetically identical cells or organisms derived from a single cell or individual by some kind of asexual reproduction

commensal.definition: either of two different animal or plant species living in close association but not interdependent

conspecific.definition: an organism belonging to the same species as another organism

denizen.definition: a plant or animal naturalized in a region

diploid.definition: (genetics) an organism or cell having the normal amount of DNA per cell; i.e., two sets of chromosomes or twice the haploid number

dwarf (organism).definition: a plant or animal that is atypically small

eukaryote.definition: an organism with cells characteristic of all life forms except primitive microorganisms such as bacteria; i.e. an organism with `good' or membrane-bound nuclei in its cells

fungus.definition: an organism of the kingdom Fungi lacking chlorophyll and feeding on organic matter; ranging from unicellular or multicellular organisms to spore-bearing syncytia

agaric (fungus).definition: fungus used in the preparation of punk for fuses

ascomycete.definition: any fungus of the class Ascomycetes (or subdivision Ascomycota) in which the spores are formed inside an ascus

clavicipitaceae.definition: any of various mushrooms of the class Ascomycetes

grainy_club.definition: a variety of grainy club mushrooms

discomycete.definition: any fungus that is a member of the subclass Discomycetes

aleuria_aurantia.definition: a discomycete with bright orange cup-shaped or saucer-shaped fruiting bodies and pale orange exteriors

blood_cup.definition: a scarlet European fungus with cup-shaped ascocarp

caloscypha_fulgens.definition: an early spring variety of discomycete with yellow to orange yellow lining of the cup

galiella_rufa.definition: the cup-shaped fruiting body of this discomycete has a jellylike interior and a short stalk

jafnea_semitosta.definition: the fruiting bodies of this discomycete have a firm texture and long retain their cup shape; the pale brown interior blends with the color of dead leaves

leotia_lubrica.definition: a discomycete that develops in clusters of slippery rubbery gelatinous fruiting bodies that are dingy yellow to tan in color

mitrula_elegans.definition: a discomycete that is 3-8 cm high with an orange to yellow fertile portion and white or pinkish stalks often half in and half out of the water

peziza_domicilina.definition: a discomycetous fungus of the genus Peziza; the fragile fruiting body is a ghostly white but stains yellow when broken; favors strongly alkaline habitats

sarcoscypha_coccinea.definition: a discomycete that is a harbinger of spring; the fruiting body is thin and tough and saucer-shaped (about the size of quarter to a half dollar) with a deep bright red upper surface and a whitish exterior

urnula_craterium.definition: an urn-shaped discomycete with a nearly black interior

black_felt_cup.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

charred_pancake_cup.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

devil's_cigar.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

devil's_urn.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

rufous_rubber_cup.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

winter_urn.definition: a common name for a variety of Sarcosomataceae

aspergillus_fumigatus.definition: a mold causing aspergillosis in birds and man

basidiomycete.definition: any of various fungi of the subdivision Basidiomycota

agaric (basidiomycete).definition: a saprophytic fungus of the order Agaricales having an umbrellalike cap with gills on the underside

armillaria_caligata.definition: fungus with a brown cap and white gills and a membranous ring halfway up the stalk

armillaria_ponderosa.definition: a large white mushroom that develops brown stains as it ages; gills are white; odor is spicy and aromatic; collected commercially for oriental cooking the Pacific Northwest

armillaria_zelleri.definition: a large fungus with viscid cap that dries and turns brown with age; gills are off-white

blewits.definition: edible agaric that is pale lilac when young; has a smooth moist cap

blushing_mushroom.definition: yellowish edible agaric that usually turns red when touched

chanterelle.definition: widely distributed edible mushroom rich yellow in color with a smooth cap and a pleasant apricot aroma

chlorophyllum_molybdites.definition: a poisonous agaric with a fibrillose cap and brown scales on a white ground color; cap can reach a diameter of 30 cm; often forms `fairy rings'

cinnabar_chanterelle.definition: mushroom with a distinctive pink to vermillion fruiting body

clitocybe_clavipes.definition: an agaric with a flat cap that is greyish or yellowish brown with pallid gills and a stalk that bulges toward the base

clitocybe_dealbata.definition: a small poisonous agaric; has a dry white cap with crowded gills and a short stalk

clitocybe_inornata.definition: a fungus with a cap that is creamy grey when young and turns brown with age and a whitish stalk that stains yellow when handled

clitocybe_irina.definition: an edible agaric with large silky white caps and thick stalks

clitocybe_robusta.definition: a large white agaric; edible but not palatable

clitocybe_subconnexa.definition: an edible white agaric that fruits in dense clusters; the gills are narrow and crowded and the stalk is fleshy and unpolished
