white-rayed_mule's_ears.definition: herb with basal leaves and leafy hairy stems bearing solitary flower heads with white or pale cream-colored rays; northwestern United States

wild_carrot.definition: a widely naturalized Eurasian herb with finely cut foliage and white compound umbels of small white or yellowish flowers and thin yellowish roots

woolly_daisy.definition: tiny grey woolly tufted annual with small golden-yellow flower heads; southeastern California to northwestern Arizona and southwestern Utah; sometimes placed in genus Eriophyllum

woolly_sunflower.definition: any plant of the genus Eriophyllum

golden_yarrow.definition: greyish woolly leafy perennial with branched stems ending in leafless stalks bearing golden-yellow flower heads; dry areas western North America

yellow_salsify.definition: European perennial naturalized throughout United States having hollow stems with a few long narrow tapered leaves and each bearing a solitary pale yellow flower

polymorph.definition: an organism that can assume more than one adult form as in the castes of ants or termites

polyploid.definition: (genetics) an organism or cell having more than twice the haploid number of chromosomes

prokaryote.definition: a unicellular organism having cells lacking membrane-bound nuclei; bacteria are the prime example but also included are blue-green algae and actinomycetes and mycoplasma

relative (organism).definition: an animal or plant that bears a relationship to another (as related by common descent or by membership in the same genus)

relict (organism).definition: an organism or species surviving as a remnant of an otherwise extinct flora or fauna in an environment much changed from that in which it originated

saprobe.definition: an organism that lives in and derives its nourishment from organic matter in stagnant or foul water

saprophyte.definition: an organism that feeds on dead organic matter especially a fungus or bacterium

sitter.definition: an organism (person or animal) that sits

stander.definition: an organism (person or animal) that stands

standee (stander).definition: someone who stands in a place where one might otherwise sit (as a spectator who uses standing room in a theater or a passenger on a crowded bus or train)

utterer (organism).definition: an organism that can utter vocal sounds

zooid.definition: one of the distinct individuals forming a colonial animal such as a bryozoan or hydrozoan

natural_object.definition: an object occurring naturally; not made by man

asterism.definition: (astronomy) a cluster of stars (or a small constellation)

black_body.definition: a hypothetical object capable of absorbing all the electromagnetic radiation falling on it

human_body.definition: alternative names for the body of a human being

adult_body.definition: the body of an adult human being

female_body.definition: the body of a female human being

adult_female_body.definition: the body of an adult woman

juvenile_body.definition: the body of a young person

child's_body.definition: the body of a human child

male_body.definition: the body of a male human being

adult_male_body.definition: the body of an adult man

person (human_body).definition: a human body (usually including the clothing)

life_form.definition: the characteristic bodily form of a mature organism

live_body.definition: the body of a living animal or person

system (live_body).definition: the living body considered as made up of interdependent components forming a unified whole

cadaver.definition: the dead body of a human being

cremains.definition: the remains of a dead body after cremation

carcase.definition: the dead body of an animal especially one slaughtered and dressed for food

carrion.definition: the dead and rotting body of an animal; unfit for human food

mummy.definition: a body embalmed and dried and wrapped for burial (as in ancient Egypt)

roadkill.definition: the dead body of an animal that has been killed on a road by a vehicle

chromosome.definition: a threadlike strand of DNA in the cell nucleus that carries the genes in a linear order

acrocentric_chromosome.definition: a chromosome with the centromere near one end so that one chromosomal arm is short and one is long

autosome.definition: any chromosome that is not a sex chromosome; appear in pairs in body cells but as single chromosomes in spermatozoa

metacentric_chromosome.definition: a chromosome having two equal arms because the centromere is in median position

sex_chromosome.definition: (genetics) a chromosome that determines the sex of an individual

x_chromosome.definition: the sex chromosome that is present in both sexes: singly in males and doubly in females

xx.definition: (genetics) normal complement of sex chromosomes in a female

xxx.definition: (genetics) abnormal complement of three X chromosomes in a female

xxy.definition: (genetics) abnormal complement of sex hormones in a male resulting in Klinefelter's syndrome

xy.definition: (genetics) normal complement of sex hormones in a male

xyy.definition: (genetics) abnormal complement of sex hormones in a male who has two Y chromosomes

y_chromosome.definition: the sex chromosome that is carried by men

telocentric_chromosome.definition: a chromosome like a straight rod with the centromere in terminal position

inclusion_body.definition: any small intracellular body found within another (characteristic of certain diseases)

plasmid.definition: a small cellular inclusion consisting of a ring of DNA that is not in a chromosome but is capable of autonomous replication

russell's_body.definition: an inclusion body found in plasma cells in cases of cancer

mass.definition: a body of matter without definite shape

coprolith.definition: a hard mass of fecal matter

drift (mass).definition: a large mass of material that is heaped up by the wind or by water currents

snowdrift.definition: a mass of snow heaped up by the wind

mat (mass).definition: a mass that is densely tangled or interwoven

particle.definition: a body having finite mass and internal structure but negligible dimensions

alpha_particle.definition: a positively charged particle that is the nucleus of the helium atom; emitted from natural or radioactive isotopes

beta_particle.definition: a high-speed electron or positron emitted in the decay of a radioactive isotope

boson.definition: any particle that obeys Bose-Einstein statistics but not the Pauli exclusion principle; all nuclei with an even mass number are bosons

gauge_boson.definition: a particle that mediates the interaction of two elementary particles

gluon.definition: a gauge boson that mediates strong interaction among quarks

graviton.definition: a gauge boson that mediates the (extremely weak) gravitational interactions between particles

intermediate_vector_boson.definition: a gauge boson that mediates weak interactions between particles

photon.definition: a quantum of electromagnetic radiation; an elementary particle that is its own antiparticle

deuteron.definition: the nucleus of deuterium; consists of one proton and one neutron; used as a bombarding particle in accelerators

elementary_particle.definition: (physics) a particle that is less complex than an atom; regarded as constituents of all matter

antimuon.definition: the antiparticle of a muon; decays to positron and neutrino and antineutrino

antitauon.definition: an antilepton of very great mass

positron.definition: an elementary particle with positive charge; interaction of a positron and an electron results in annihilation

antiparticle.definition: a particle that has the same mass as another particle but has opposite values for its other properties; interaction of a particle and its antiparticle results in annihilation and the production of radiant energy

hadron.definition: any elementary particle that interacts strongly with other particles

meson.definition: an elementary particle responsible for the forces in the atomic nucleus; a hadron with a baryon number of 0

j_particle.definition: a neutral meson with a large mass

kaon.definition: an unstable meson produced as the result of a high-energy particle collision

pion.definition: a meson involved in holding the nucleus together; produced as the result of high-energy particle collision

antibaryon.definition: the antiparticle of a baryon; a hadron with a baryon number of -1

quark.definition: (physics) hypothetical truly fundamental particle in mesons and baryons; there are supposed to be six flavors of quarks (and their antiquarks), which come in pairs; each has an electric charge of +2/3 or -1/3

bottom_quark.definition: a quark with a charge of -1/3 and a mass about 10,000 times that of an electron

charm_quark.definition: a quark with an electric charge of +2/3 and a mass 2900 times that of an electron and a charm of +1

down_quark.definition: a stable quark with an electric charge of -1/3 and a mass 607 times that of an electron

strange_quark.definition: a quark with an electric charge of -1/3 and a mass 988 times that of an electron and a strangeness of -1

top_quark.definition: a hypothetical quark with a charge of +2/3 and a mass more than 100,000 times that of an electron

up_quark.definition: a stable quark with an electric charge of +2/3 and a mass 607 times that of an electron

strange_particle.definition: an elementary particle with non-zero strangeness

string.definition: (cosmology) a hypothetical one-dimensional subatomic particle having a concentration of energy and the dynamic properties of a flexible loop

weakly_interacting_massive_particle.definition: a hypothetical subatomic particle of large mass that interacts weakly with ordinary matter through gravitation; postulated as a constituent of the dark matter of the universe

fermion.definition: any particle that obeys Fermi-Dirac statistics and is subject to the Pauli exclusion principle

baryon.definition: any of the elementary particles having a mass equal to or greater than that of a proton and that participate in strong interactions; a hadron with a baryon number of +1

hyperon.definition: any baryon that is not a nucleon; unstable particle with mass greater than a neutron

lambda_particle.definition: an electrically neutral baryon with isotopic spin 1

nucleon.definition: a constituent (proton or neutron) of an atomic nucleus

antiproton.definition: an unstable negatively charged proton; the antiparticle of a proton

neutron.definition: an elementary particle with 0 charge and mass about equal to a proton; enters into the structure of the atomic nucleus

proton.definition: a stable particle with positive charge equal to the negative charge of an electron

lepton.definition: an elementary particle that participates in weak interactions; has a baryon number of 0

electron.definition: an elementary particle with negative charge

delta_ray.definition: an electron ejected from matter by ionizing radiation

free_electron.definition: electron that is not attached to an atom or ion or molecule but is free to move under the influence of an electric field

photoelectron.definition: an electron that is emitted from an atom or molecule by an incident photon

valence_electron.definition: an electron in the outer shell of an atom which can combine with other atoms to form molecules

muon.definition: an elementary particle with a negative charge and a half-life of 2 microsecond; decays to electron and neutrino and antineutrino

neutrino.definition: an elementary particle with zero charge and zero mass

tauon.definition: a lepton of very great mass

ion.definition: a particle that is electrically charged (positive or negative); an atom or molecule or group that has lost or gained one or more electrons

hydroxide_ion.definition: the anion OH having one oxygen and one hydrogen atom

hydrogen_ion.definition: a positively charged atom of hydrogen; that is to say, a normal hydrogen atomic nucleus

diazonium.definition: the univalent cation R-N:N- (where R is an aromatic hydrocarbon); found in salts that are used in manufacturing azo dyes

magnetic_monopole.definition: a hypothetical particle with a single magnetic pole instead of the usual two

micelle.definition: an electrically charged particle built up from polymeric molecules or ions and occurring in certain colloidal electrolytic solutions like soaps and detergents

prion.definition: (microbiology) an infectious protein particle similar to a virus but lacking nucleic acid; thought to be the agent responsible for scrapie and other degenerative diseases of the nervous system

superstring.definition: a hypothetical particle that is the elementary particle in a theory of space-time

thermion.definition: an electrically charged particle (electron or ion) emitted by a substance at a high temperature

virino.definition: (microbiology) a hypothetical infectious particle thought to be the cause of scrapie and other degenerative diseases of the central nervous system; consists of nucleic acid in a protective coat of host cell proteins

virion.definition: (virology) a complete viral particle; nucleic acid and capsid (and a lipid envelope in some viruses)

carpet.definition: a natural object that resembles or suggests a carpet

celestial_body.definition: natural objects visible in the sky

minor_planet.definition: any of numerous small celestial bodies that move around the sun

asteroid.definition: any of numerous small celestial bodies composed of rock and metal that move around the sun (mainly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter)

chiron.definition: an asteroid discovered in 1977; it is unique in having an orbit lying mainly between the orbits of Saturn and Uranus

kuiper_belt_object.definition: any of many minor planets in the Kuiper belt outside the orbit of Neptune at the edge of the solar system

inferior_planet.definition: any of the planets whose orbit lies inside the earth's orbit

jovian_planet.definition: any of the four outermost planets in the solar system; much larger than Earth and gaseous in nature (like Jupiter)

morning_star.definition: a planet (usually Venus) seen just before sunrise in the eastern sky

outer_planet.definition: (astronomy) a major planet whose orbit is outside the asteroid belt (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto)

superior_planet.definition: any of the planets whose orbit lies outside the earth's orbit

terrestrial_planet.definition: a planet having a compact rocky surface like the Earth's; the four innermost planets in the solar system

planetesimal.definition: one of many small solid celestial bodies thought to have existed at an early stage in the development of the solar system

primary (celestial_body).definition: (astronomy) a celestial body (especially a star) relative to other objects in orbit around it

quasar.definition: a starlike object that may send out radio waves and other forms of energy; many have large red shifts

satellite (celestial_body).definition: any celestial body orbiting around a planet or star

galilean_satellite.definition: one of the four satellites of Jupiter that were discovered by Galileo

moon (satellite).definition: any natural satellite of a planet

binary_star.definition: a system of two stars that revolve around each other under their mutual gravitation

fixed_star.definition: any star in the Ptolemaic theory of planetary motion

giant_star.definition: a very bright star of large diameter and low density (relative to the Sun)

lodestar.definition: guiding star; a star that is used as a reference point in navigation or astronomy

multiple_star.definition: a system of three or more stars associated by gravity

trapezium.definition: a multiple star in the constellation of Orion

neutron_star.definition: a star that has collapsed under its own gravity; it is composed of neutrons

pulsar.definition: a degenerate neutron star; small and extremely dense; rotates very fast and emits regular pulses of polarized radiation

nova.definition: a star that ejects some of its material in the form of a cloud and become more luminous in the process

red_dwarf.definition: a small, old, relatively cool star; approximately 100 times the mass of Jupiter

flare_star.definition: a red dwarf star in which luminosity can change several magnitudes in a few minutes

red_giant.definition: a large, old, luminous star; has a relatively low surface temperature and a diameter large relative to the sun

sun (star).definition: any star around which a planetary system revolves

supergiant.definition: an extremely bright star of very large diameter and low density

supernova.definition: a star that explodes and becomes extremely luminous in the process

variable_star.definition: a star that varies noticeably in brightness

white_dwarf.definition: a faint star of enormous density

cocoon.definition: silky envelope spun by the larvae of many insects to protect pupas and by spiders to protect eggs

consolidation.definition: something that has consolidated into a compact mass

constellation.definition: a configuration of stars as seen from the earth

covering (natural_object).definition: a natural object that covers or envelops

bark (covering).definition: tough protective covering of the woody stems and roots of trees and other woody plants

angostura_bark.definition: the bitter bark of a South American tree; used in medicines and liqueurs and bitters

canella.definition: highly aromatic inner bark of the Canella winterana used as a condiment and a tonic

cascara.definition: dried bark of the cascara buckthorn used as a laxative

cascarilla_bark.definition: aromatic bark of cascarilla; used as a tonic and for making incense

cassia_bark.definition: aromatic bark of the cassia-bark tree; less desirable as a spice than Ceylon cinnamon bark

cinchona (bark).definition: medicinal bark of cinchona trees; source of quinine and quinidine

cinnamon (bark).definition: aromatic bark used as a spice

cinnamon_bark.definition: aromatic bark of Saigon cinnamon used medicinally as a carminative

cork (bark).definition: outer bark of the cork oak; used for stoppers for bottles etc.

magnolia (bark).definition: dried bark of various magnolias; used in folk medicine

mezereum.definition: the dried bark of the shrub mezereon

phellem.definition: (botany) outer tissue of bark; a protective layer of dead cells

tanbark.definition: bark rich in tannin; bruised and cut in pieces to use for tanning; spent tanbark used as a ground covering

tapa (bark).definition: the thin fibrous bark of the paper mulberry and Pipturus albidus

winter's_bark (bark).definition: aromatic bark having tonic and stimulant properties

body_covering.definition: any covering for the body or a body part

epicranium.definition: the muscle and aponeurosis and skin covering the cranium

exoskeleton.definition: the exterior protective or supporting structure or shell of many animals (especially invertebrates) including bony or horny parts such as nails or scales or hoofs

plastron (exoskeleton).definition: (zoology) the part of a turtle's shell forming its underside

exuviae.definition: cast-off skins or coverings of various organisms during ecdysis

feather.definition: the light horny waterproof structure forming the external covering of birds

aftershaft.definition: a supplementary feather (usually small) on the underside of the base of the shaft of some feathers in some birds

bastard_wing.definition: tuft of small stiff feathers on the first digit of a bird's wing

contour_feather.definition: feathers covering the body of an adult bird and determining its shape

plumule.definition: down feather of young birds; persists in some adult birds

flight_feather.definition: any of the larger wing or tail feathers of a bird

primary (flight_feather).definition: one of the main flight feathers projecting along the outer edge of a bird's wing

tail_feather.definition: feather growing from the tail (uropygium) of a bird

sickle_feather.definition: one of the long curved tail feathers of a rooster

hackle.definition: long slender feather on the necks of e.g. turkeys and pheasants

saddle_hackle.definition: a long narrow feather on the back (saddle) of a domestic fowl

marabou (feather).definition: the downy feathers of marabou storks are used for trimming garments

scapular (feather).definition: a feather covering the shoulder of a bird

hair.definition: a covering for the body (or parts of it) consisting of a dense growth of threadlike structures (as on the human head); helps to prevent heat loss

beard (hair).definition: hairy growth on or near the face of certain mammals

body_hair.definition: short hair growing over a person's body

coat (hair).definition: growth of hair or wool or fur covering the body of an animal

fur (coat).definition: dense coat of fine silky hairs on mammals (e.g., cat or seal or weasel)

undercoat (fur).definition: thick soft fur lying beneath the longer and coarser guard hair

wool (coat).definition: outer coat of especially sheep and yaks

cowlick.definition: a tuft of hair that grows in a different direction from the rest of the hair and usually will not lie flat

down (hair).definition: fine soft dense hair (as the fine short hair of cattle or deer or the wool of sheep or the undercoat of certain dogs)

lanugo.definition: the fine downy hair covering a human fetus; normally shed during the ninth month of gestation

eyebrow.definition: the arch of hair above each eye

eyelash.definition: any of the short curved hairs that grow from the edges of the eyelids

facial_hair.definition: hair on the face (especially on the face of a man)

beard (facial_hair).definition: the hair growing on the lower part of a man's face

fuzz.definition: the first beard of an adolescent boy

goatee.definition: a small chin beard trimmed to a point; named for its resemblance to a goat's beard

imperial (beard).definition: a small tufted beard worn by Emperor Napoleon III

soul_patch.definition: a small patch of facial hair just below the lower lip and above the chin

stubble.definition: short stiff hairs growing on a man's face when he has not shaved for a few days

vandyke_beard.definition: a short pointed beard (named after the artist Anthony Vandyke)

mustache.definition: an unshaved growth of hair on the upper lip

mustachio.definition: a large bushy moustache (with hair growing sometimes down the sides of the mouth)

sideburn.definition: facial hair that has grown down the side of a man's face in front of the ears (especially when the rest of the beard is shaved off)

forelock (hair).definition: a lock of a horse's mane that grows forward between the ears

guard_hair.definition: coarse hairs that form the outer fur and protect the underfur of certain mammals

hairdo.definition: the arrangement of the hair (especially a woman's hair)

bang.definition: a border of hair that is cut short and hangs across the forehead

bob (hairdo).definition: a hair style for women and children; a short haircut all around

bouffant.definition: a woman's hairstyle in which the hair gives a puffy appearance

braid (hairdo).definition: a hairdo formed by braiding or twisting the hair

queue.definition: a braid of hair at the back of the head

chignon.definition: a roll of hair worn at the nape of the neck

haircut.definition: the style in which hair has been cut

brush_cut.definition: a short haircut with hairs standing up like a brush

crew_cut.definition: a closely cropped haircut; usually for men

mohawk (haircut).definition: haircut in which the head is shaved except for a band of hair down the middle of the scalp

marcel.definition: a hairdo characterized by deep regular waves that are made by a heated curling iron

pageboy.definition: a smooth hair style with the ends of the hair curled inward

pompadour.definition: a hair style in which the front hair is swept up from the forehead

ponytail.definition: a hair style that draws the hair back so that it hangs down in back of the head like a pony's tail

roach (hairdo).definition: a roll of hair brushed back from the forehead

scalp_lock.definition: a long tuft of hair left on top of the shaven head

wave (hairdo).definition: a hairdo that creates undulations in the hair

finger_wave.definition: a wave made with the fingers

permanent_wave.definition: a series of waves in the hair made by applying heat and chemicals

lock (hair).definition: a strand or cluster of hair

crimp (lock).definition: a lock of hair that has been artificially waved or curled

pin_curl.definition: a curl of hair made by dampening a strand of hair and curling it and holding the curl with a clip or bobby pin

spit_curl.definition: a spiral curl plastered on the forehead or cheek

dreadlock.definition: one of many long thin braids of hair radiating from the scalp; popularized by Rastafarians

forelock (lock).definition: a lock of hair growing (or falling) over the forehead

quiff.definition: a prominent forelock (especially one brushed upward from the forehead)

pubic_hair.definition: hair growing in the pubic area

minge.definition: vulgar term for a woman's pubic hair or genitals

headful.definition: a covering over the surface of your head

hide.definition: body covering of a living animal

protective_covering (body_covering).definition: the tough natural covering of some organisms

clypeus.definition: a shield-like plate on the front of an insect's head

sclerite.definition: hard plate or element of the exoskeleton of some arthropods

scute.definition: large bony or horny plate as on an armadillo or turtle or the underside of a snake

carapace.definition: hard outer covering or case of certain organisms such as arthropods and turtles

cuticula.definition: the outer body wall of an insect

skin (body_covering).definition: a natural protective body covering and site of the sense of touch

cuticle.definition: the dead skin at the base of a fingernail or toenail

dewlap.definition: a hanging fold of loose skin on an elderly person's neck

hangnail.definition: a loose narrow strip of skin near the base of a fingernail; tearing it produces a painful sore that is easily infected

investment.definition: outer layer or covering of an organ or part or organism

pellicle.definition: thin protective membrane in some protozoa

scalp.definition: the skin that covers the top of the head

skin_graft.definition: a piece of skin taken from a donor area and surgically grafted at the site of an injury or burn

thick_skin.definition: skin that is very thick (as an elephant or rhinoceros)

crust (covering).definition: a hard outer layer that covers something

tartar.definition: an incrustation that forms on the teeth and gums

envelope (covering).definition: a natural covering (as by a fluid)

hood (covering).definition: a protective covering that is part of a plant

indumentum.definition: a covering of fine hairs (or sometimes scales) as on a leaf or insect

indusium.definition: a membrane enclosing and protecting the developing spores especially that covering the sori of a fern

integument.definition: an outer protective covering such as the skin of an animal or a cuticle or seed coat or rind or shell

pericarp.definition: the ripened and variously modified walls of a plant ovary

bur (pericarp).definition: seed vessel having hooks or prickles

capsule (pericarp).definition: a dry dehiscent seed vessel or the spore-containing structure of e.g. mosses

bilocular_capsule.definition: a capsule divided into two cells or compartments

boll.definition: the rounded seed-bearing capsule of a cotton or flax plant

silique.definition: narrow elongated seed capsule peculiar to the family Cruciferae

silicle.definition: short broad silique occurring in some cruciferous plants

epicarp.definition: outermost layer of the pericarp of fruits as the skin of a peach or grape

mesocarp.definition: the middle layer of a pericarp

stone (pericarp).definition: the hard inner (usually woody) layer of the pericarp of some fruits (as peaches or plums or cherries or olives) that contains the seed

cherry_stone.definition: the stone seed of a cherry

peach_pit.definition: the stone seed of a peach

peridium.definition: outer layer of the spore-bearing organ in many fungi

roof.definition: the inner top surface of a covered area or hollow space

scale (covering).definition: a flattened rigid plate forming part of the body covering of many animals

fish_scale.definition: scale of the kind that covers the bodies of fish

squama.definition: a protective structure resembling a scale

alula.definition: scalelike structure between the base of the wing and the halter of a two-winged fly

sheath (covering).definition: an enveloping structure or covering enclosing an animal or plant organ or part

husk.definition: outer membranous covering of some fruits or seeds

bract.definition: a modified leaf or leaflike part just below and protecting an inflorescence

epicalyx.definition: a group of bracts simulating a calyx as in a carnation or hibiscus

glume.definition: small dry membranous bract found in inflorescences of Gramineae and Cyperaceae

lemma.definition: the lower and stouter of the two glumes immediately enclosing the floret in most Gramineae

involucre.definition: a highly conspicuous bract or bract pair or ring of bracts at the base of an inflorescence

spathe.definition: a conspicuous bract surrounding or subtending a spadix or other inflorescence

cornhusk.definition: the husk of an ear of corn

hull (husk).definition: dry outer covering of a fruit or seed or nut

shell (hull).definition: the hard usually fibrous outer layer of some fruits especially nuts

nutshell.definition: the shell around the kernel of a nut

pod (husk).definition: the vessel that contains the seeds of a plant (not the seeds themselves)

pea_pod.definition: husk of a pea; edible in some garden peas

lorica.definition: a hard protective sheath (as secreted by certain protoctists, for example)

medullary_sheath.definition: a layer of myelin encasing (and insulating) the axons of medullated nerve fibers

neurolemma.definition: thin membranous sheath around a nerve fiber

theca (sheath).definition: outer sheath of the pupa of certain insects

phragmocone.definition: the thin conical chambered internal shell (either straight or curved) of a belemnite

seashell.definition: the shell of a marine organism

skim.definition: a thin layer covering the surface of a liquid

slough (covering).definition: any outer covering that can be shed or cast off (such as the cast-off skin of a snake)

snowcap.definition: a covering of snow (as on a mountain peak)

test.definition: a hard outer covering as of some amoebas and sea urchins

theca (covering).definition: a case or sheath especially a pollen sac or moss capsule

vesture.definition: something that covers or cloaks like a garment

extraterrestrial_object.definition: a natural object existing outside the earth and outside the earth's atmosphere

comet.definition: (astronomy) a relatively small extraterrestrial body consisting of a frozen mass that travels around the sun in a highly elliptical orbit

meteoroid.definition: (astronomy) any of the small solid extraterrestrial bodies that hits the earth's atmosphere

meteor_swarm.definition: a group of meteoroids with similar paths

meteorite.definition: stony or metallic object that is the remains of a meteoroid that has reached the earth's surface

aerolite.definition: a stony meteorite consisting of silicate minerals

micrometeorite.definition: a meteorite or meteoroid so small that it drifts down to earth without becoming intensely heated in the atmosphere

pallasite.definition: a meteorite composed principally of olivine and metallic iron

siderite.definition: a meteorite consisting principally of nickel and iron

mechanism (natural_object).definition: a natural object resembling a machine in structure or function

barrier (mechanism).definition: anything serving to maintain separation by obstructing vision or access

bar (barrier).definition: a submerged (or partly submerged) ridge in a river or along a shore

blood-brain_barrier.definition: a mechanism that creates a barrier between brain tissues and circulating blood; serves to protect the central nervous system

curtain (barrier).definition: any barrier to communication or vision

biological_clock.definition: an innate mechanism in living organisms that controls the periodicity of many physiological functions

transmission_mechanism.definition: any mechanism whereby an infectious agent is spread from a reservoir to a human being

airborne_transmission.definition: a transmission mechanism in the which the infectious agent is spread as an aerosol and usually enters a person through the respiratory tract

direct_transmission.definition: a transmission mechanism in which the infectious agent is transferred directly into the body via touching or biting or kissing or sexual intercourse or by droplets entering the eye or nose or mouth

indirect_transmission.definition: a transmission mechanism in which the infectious agent is transferred to the person by a fomite of vector

vector-borne_transmission.definition: indirect transmission of an infectious agent that occurs when a vector bites or touches a person

vehicle-borne_transmission.definition: indirect transmission of an infectious agent that occurs when a vehicle (or fomite) touches a person's body or is ingested

nest (natural_object).definition: a structure in which animals lay eggs or give birth to their young

beehive (nest).definition: a structure that provides a natural habitation for bees; as in a hollow tree

bird's_nest.definition: nest where birds lay their eggs and hatch their young

aerie (bird's_nest).definition: the lofty nest of a bird of prey (such as a hawk or eagle)

mouse_nest.definition: where mice bear and raise their young

nidus.definition: a nest in which spiders or insects deposit their eggs

plant_part.definition: any part of a plant or fungus

annulus.definition: (Fungi) a remnant of the partial veil that in mature mushrooms surrounds the stem like a collar

aril.definition: fleshy and usually brightly colored cover of some seeds that develops from the ovule stalk and partially or entirely envelopes the seed

button (plant_part).definition: any of various plant parts that resemble buttons

calyptra.definition: the hood or cap covering the calyx of certain plants: e.g., the California poppy

cap (plant_part).definition: a fruiting structure resembling an umbrella or a cone that forms the top of a stalked fleshy fungus such as a mushroom

chalaza.definition: basal part of a plant ovule opposite the micropyle; where integument and nucellus are joined

corona.definition: (botany) the trumpet-shaped or cup-shaped outgrowth of the corolla of a daffodil or narcissus flower

domatium.definition: a part of a plant (e.g., a leaf) that has been modified to provide protection for insects or mites or fungi

duct (plant_part).definition: a continuous tube formed by a row of elongated cells lacking intervening end walls

germ_tube.definition: (botany) a slender tubular outgrowth from a spore in germination

gynostegium.definition: the crown of the stamen in plants of the genus Asclepias

kernel (plant_part).definition: the inner and usually edible part of a seed or grain or nut or fruit stone

ligule.definition: (botany) any appendage to a plant that is shaped like a strap

lip.definition: (botany) either of the two parts of a bilabiate corolla or calyx

lobe (plant_part).definition: (botany) a part into which a leaf is divided

mentum.definition: a projection like a chin formed by the sepals and base of the column in some orchids

mycelium.definition: the vegetative part of a fungus consisting of a mass of branching threadlike hyphae

sclerotium.definition: compact usually dark-colored mass of hardened mycelium constituting a vegetative food-storage body in various true fungi; detaches when mature and can give rise to new growth

nucellus.definition: central part of a plant ovule; contains the embryo sac

plant_organ.definition: a functional and structural unit of a plant or fungus

perianth.definition: collective term for the outer parts of a flower consisting of the calyx and corolla and enclosing the stamens and pistils

falls.definition: the petals or sepals of a flower that bend downward (especially the outer perianth of an iris)

archegonium.definition: a female sex organ occurring in mosses, ferns, and most gymnosperms

capitulum (plant_organ).definition: a dense cluster of flowers or foliage

cupule.definition: cup-shaped structure of hardened bracts at the base of an acorn

fruiting_body.definition: an organ specialized for producing spores

acervulus.definition: small asexual fruiting body resembling a cushion or blister consisting of a mat of hyphae that is produced on a host by some fungi

aecium.definition: fruiting body of some rust fungi bearing chains of aeciospores

ascocarp.definition: mature fruiting body of an ascomycetous fungus

apothecium.definition: a cuplike ascocarp in many lichens and ascomycetous fungi

elf_cup.definition: apothecium of a fungus of the family Pezizaceae

ascoma.definition: an ascocarp having the spore-bearing layer of cells (the hymenium) on a broad disklike receptacle

cleistothecium.definition: closed spore-bearing structure of some fungi (especially Aspergillaceae and Erysiphaceae) from which spores are released only by decay or disintegration

basidiocarp.definition: the fruiting body of a basidiomycete which bears its spores on special cells

galea.definition: an organ shaped like a helmet; usually a vaulted and enlarged petal as in Aconitum

gill.definition: any of the radiating leaflike spore-producing structures on the underside of the cap of a mushroom or similar fungus

hypanthium.definition: the cuplike or ringlike or tubular structure of a flower which bears the sepals and stamens and calyx (as in Rosaceae)

hypobasidium.definition: special cell constituting the base of the basidium in various fungi especially of the order Tremellales

leaf (plant_organ).definition: the main organ of photosynthesis and transpiration in higher plants

amplexicaul_leaf.definition: a leaf with its base clasping the stem

blade (leaf).definition: especially a leaf of grass or the broad portion of a leaf as distinct from the petiole

cataphyll.definition: a reduced or scarcely developed leaf at the start of a plant's life (i.e., cotyledons) or in the early stages of leaf development

compound_leaf.definition: a leaf composed of a number of leaflets on a common stalk

decompound_leaf.definition: a leaf having divisions that are themselves compound

palmate_leaf.definition: a leaf resembling an open hand; having lobes radiating from a common point

pedate_leaf.definition: a leaf having the radiating lobes each deeply cleft or divided

pinnate_leaf.definition: a leaf resembling a feather; having the leaflets on each side of a common axis

bijugate_leaf.definition: a pinnate leaf having two pairs of leaflets

bipinnate_leaf.definition: a leaf having pinnate leaflets; as ferns

even-pinnate_leaf.definition: a pinnate leaf with a pair of leaflets at the apex

odd-pinnate_leaf.definition: a pinnate leaf with a single leaflet at the apex

quinquefoliate_leaf.definition: a compound leaf having five leaflets

crenate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a scalloped margin

dandelion_green.definition: the foliage of the dandelion plant

dentate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a toothed margin

denticulate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a finely toothed margin; minutely dentate

emarginate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a notch at the apex

entire_leaf.definition: a leaf having a smooth margin without notches or indentations

erose_leaf.definition: a leaf having a jagged margin as though gnawed

fig_leaf (leaf).definition: a leaf from a fig tree

floral_leaf.definition: a modified leaf that is part of a flower

petal.definition: part of the perianth that is usually brightly colored

sepal.definition: one of the green parts that form the calyx of a flower

frond.definition: compound leaf of a fern or palm or cycad

pinna.definition: division of a usually pinnately divided leaf

lobed_leaf.definition: a leaf having deeply indented margins

pad (leaf).definition: the large floating leaf of an aquatic plant (as the water lily)

lily_pad.definition: floating leaves of a water lily

parallel-veined_leaf.definition: a leaf whose veins run in parallel from the stem

parted_leaf.definition: a leaf having margins incised almost to the base so as to create distinct divisions or lobes

pitcher (leaf).definition: (botany) a leaf that that is modified in such a way as to resemble a pitcher or ewer

rosette (leaf).definition: a cluster of leaves growing in crowded circles from a common center or crown (usually at or close to the ground)

runcinate_leaf.definition: a leaf having incised margins with the lobes or teeth curved toward the base; as a dandelion leaf

scale (leaf).definition: a specialized leaf or bract that protects a bud or catkin

serrate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a margin notched like a saw with teeth pointing toward the apex

simple_leaf.definition: a leaf that is not divided into parts

acuminate_leaf.definition: a leaf narrowing to a slender point

cuneate_leaf.definition: a wedge-shaped leaf having the acute angle at the base

deltoid_leaf.definition: a simple leaf shaped like a capital delta

elliptic_leaf.definition: a simple leaf shaped like an ellipse

ensiform_leaf.definition: a sword-shaped leaf; as of iris

hastate_leaf.definition: a leaf shaped like a spearhead with flaring pointed lobes at the base

lanceolate_leaf.definition: a leaf shaped like a lance head; tapering to a point at each end

lyrate_leaf.definition: a simple leaf having curvature suggestive of a lyre

oblanceolate_leaf.definition: a leaf having a rounded apex and tapering base

oblong_leaf.definition: a simple leaf that is rounded at each end with parallel sides

obovate_leaf.definition: an egg-shaped leaf with the narrower end at the base

obtuse_leaf.definition: a simple leaf having a rounded or blunt tip

ovate_leaf.definition: an egg-shaped leaf with the broader end at the base

peltate_leaf.definition: a shield-shaped leaf; as a nasturtium leaf

perfoliate_leaf.definition: a leaf with the base united around--and apparently pierced by--the stem

sagittate-leaf.definition: a leaf shaped like an arrow head

spatulate_leaf.definition: spatula-shaped leaf; having a broad rounded apex and narrow base

sporophyll.definition: leaf in ferns and mosses that bears the sporangia

megasporophyll.definition: in non-flowering plants, a sporophyll that bears only megasporangia

microsporophyll.definition: in non-flowering plants, a sporophyll that bears only microsporangia

mescal_button.definition: the button-shaped top of the mescal cactus; a source of psilocybin

nectary.definition: a gland (often a protuberance or depression) that secretes nectar

reproductive_structure.definition: the parts of a plant involved in its reproduction

spore.definition: a small usually single-celled asexual reproductive body produced by many nonflowering plants and fungi and some bacteria and protozoans and that are capable of developing into a new individual without sexual fusion

aeciospore.definition: spore of a rust fungus formed in an aecium

ascospore.definition: sexually produced fungal spore formed within an ascus

stamen.definition: the male reproductive organ of a flower

stigma.definition: the apical end of the style where deposited pollen enters the pistil

style.definition: (botany) the narrow elongated part of the pistil between the ovary and the stigma

cornsilk.definition: each of the long filamentous styles that grow as a silky tuft at the tip of an ear of Indian corn

stylopodium.definition: an enlargement at the base of the style in some Umbelliferae

testa.definition: protective outer layer of seeds of flowering plants

root.definition: (botany) the usually underground organ that lacks buds or leaves or nodes; absorbs water and mineral salts; usually it anchors the plant to the ground

adventitious_root.definition: root growing in an unusual location e.g. from a stem

briarroot.definition: hard woody root of the briar Erica arborea

calamus (root).definition: the aromatic root of the sweet flag used medicinally

carrot (root).definition: deep orange edible root of the cultivated carrot plant

cassava (root).definition: cassava root eaten as a staple food after drying and leaching; source of tapioca

chicory (root).definition: the dried root of the chicory plant: used as a coffee substitute

horseradish (root).definition: the root of the horseradish plant; it is grated or ground and used for seasoning

licorice_root.definition: root of licorice used in flavoring e.g. candy and liqueurs and medicines

mandrake_root.definition: the root of the mandrake plant; used medicinally or as a narcotic

orrisroot.definition: fragrant rootstock of various irises especially Florentine iris; used in perfumes and medicines

parsnip (root).definition: the whitish root of cultivated parsnip

pneumatophore.definition: an air-filled root (submerged or exposed) that can function as a respiratory organ of a marsh or swamp plant

prop_root.definition: a root that grows from and supports the stem above the ground in plants such as mangroves

radish.definition: pungent edible root of any of various cultivated radish plants

rootlet.definition: small root or division of a root

salsify (root).definition: edible root of the salsify plant

sarsaparilla_root.definition: dried root of any of various plants of the genus Smilax used as a flavoring agent

senega (root).definition: dried root of two plants of the genus Polygala containing an irritating saponin

taproot.definition: (botany) main root of a plant growing straight downward from the stem

taro (root).definition: edible starchy tuberous root of taro plants

root_cap.definition: thimble-shaped mass of cells covering and protecting the growing tip of a root

root_hair.definition: thin hairlike outgrowth of an epidermal cell just behind the tip; absorbs nutrients from the soil

septum.definition: a partition or wall especially in an ovary

sprout.definition: any new growth of a plant such as a new branch or a bud

bud (sprout).definition: a swelling on a plant stem consisting of overlapping immature leaves or petals

flower_bud.definition: a bud from which only a flower or flowers develop

clove (flower_bud).definition: aromatic flower bud of a clove tree; yields a spice

leaf_bud.definition: a bud from which leaves (but not flowers) develop

mixed_bud.definition: a bud yielding both leaves and flowers

sucker (shoot).definition: a shoot arising from a plant's roots

tiller (shoot).definition: a shoot that sprouts from the base of a grass

stalk.definition: a slender or elongated structure that supports a plant or fungus or a plant part or plant organ

axis (stalk).definition: the main stem or central part about which plant organs or plant parts such as branches are arranged

rachis.definition: axis of a compound leaf or compound inflorescence

spadix.definition: the fleshy axis of a spike often surrounded by a spathe

branch.definition: a division of a stem, or secondary stem arising from the main stem of a plant

branchlet.definition: a small branch or division of a branch (especially a terminal division); usually applied to branches of the current or preceding year

wand (branchlet).definition: a thin supple twig or rod

osier (withe).definition: flexible twig of a willow tree

deadwood.definition: a branch or a part of a tree that is dead

limb (branch).definition: any of the main branches arising from the trunk or a bough of a tree

bough.definition: any of the larger branches of a tree

stick (limb).definition: a small thin branch of a tree

bulb (stalk).definition: a modified bud consisting of a thickened globular underground stem serving as a reproductive structure

bulbil.definition: small bulb or bulb-shaped growth arising from the leaf axil or in the place of flowers

onion (bulb).definition: the bulb of an onion plant

shallot (bulb).definition: aggregate bulb of the multiplier onion

squill.definition: bulb of the sea squill, which is sliced, dried, and used as an expectorant

cane (stalk).definition: a strong slender often flexible stem as of bamboos, reeds, rattans, or sugar cane

rattan (cane).definition: the stem of various climbing palms of the genus Calamus and related genera used to make wickerwork and furniture and canes

sugarcane (cane).definition: juicy canes whose sap is a source of molasses and commercial sugar; fresh canes are sometimes chewed for the juice

carpophore.definition: a slender stalk that furnishes an axis for a carpel

caudex.definition: woody stem of palms and tree ferns

cladode.definition: a flattened stem resembling and functioning as a leaf

corm.definition: solid swollen underground bulb-shaped stem or stem base and serving as a reproductive structure

cornstalk.definition: the stalk of a corn plant

culm.definition: stem of plants of the Gramineae

cutting.definition: a part (sometimes a root or leaf or bud) removed from a plant to propagate a new plant through rooting or grafting

quickset.definition: cuttings of plants set in the ground to grow as hawthorn for hedges or vines

funicle.definition: the stalk of a plant ovule or seed

gynophore.definition: the stalk of a pistil that raises it above the receptacle

haulm.definition: stems of beans and peas and potatoes and grasses collectively as used for thatching and bedding

petiole.definition: the slender stem that supports the blade of a leaf

phyllode.definition: an expanded petiole taking on the function of a leaf blade

rhizome.definition: a horizontal plant stem with shoots above and roots below serving as a reproductive structure

scape.definition: erect leafless flower stalk growing directly from the ground as in a tulip

peduncle.definition: stalk bearing an inflorescence or solitary flower

pedicel.definition: a small stalk bearing a single flower of an inflorescence; an ultimate division of a common peduncle

ray (pedicel).definition: a branch of an umbel or an umbelliform inflorescence

sporangiophore.definition: stalk bearing one or more sporangia

stipe.definition: supporting stalk or stem-like structure especially of a pistil or fern frond or supporting a mushroom cap

stock (stalk).definition: persistent thickened stem of a herbaceous perennial plant

trunk (stalk).definition: the main stem of a tree; usually covered with bark; the bole is usually the part that is commercially useful for lumber

tuber.definition: a fleshy underground stem or root serving for reproductive and food storage

groundnut (tuber).definition: nutlike tuber; important food of Native Americans

jerusalem_artichoke (tuber).definition: edible tuber of the Jerusalem artichoke

water_chestnut (tuber).definition: edible bulbous tuber of a Chinese marsh plant

yam (tuber).definition: edible tuber of any of several yams

stolon.definition: a horizontal branch from the base of plant that produces new plants from buds at its tips

cortex.definition: the tissue forming the outer layer of an organ or structure in plant or animal

adrenal_cortex.definition: the cortex of the adrenal gland; secretes corticosterone and sex hormones

renal_cortex.definition: the cortex of the kidney containing the glomeruli and the convoluted tubules

fibrous_tissue.definition: tissue consisting of or containing fibers in both animals and plants

trabecula.definition: rod-shaped structures of fibrous tissue that divide an organ into parts (as in the penis) or stabilize the structure of an organ (as in the spleen)

gall.definition: abnormal swelling of plant tissue caused by insects or microorganisms or injury

oak_apple.definition: oak gall caused by larvae of a cynipid wasp

interstitial_tissue.definition: tissue between the cells of a structure or part in plant or animal

neuroglia.definition: sustentacular tissue that surrounds and supports neurons in the central nervous system; glial and neural cells together compose the tissue of the central nervous system

astroglia.definition: tissue consisting of large stellate neuroglial cells

microglia.definition: neuroglial tissue of mesodermal origin that can become phagocytic

oligodendroglia.definition: tissue consisting of glial cells with sheetlike processes that form the myelin sheath of nerve fibers

medulla.definition: the inner part of an organ or structure in plant or animal

adrenal_medulla.definition: the medulla of the adrenal gland; secretes epinephrine

meristem.definition: undifferentiated tissue from which new cells are formed, as at the tip of a stem or root

parenchyma.definition: the primary tissue of higher plants composed of thin-walled cells that remain capable of cell division even when mature; constitutes the greater part of leaves, roots, the pulp of fruits, and the pith of stems

perisperm.definition: the nutritive tissue outside the sac containing the embryo in some seeds

pith.definition: soft spongelike central cylinder of the stems of most flowering plants

pulp (plant_tissue).definition: a soft moist part of a fruit

vascular_tissue.definition: tissue that conducts water and nutrients through the plant body in higher plants

cambium (vascular_tissue).definition: a formative one-cell layer of tissue between xylem and phloem in most vascular plants that is responsible for secondary growth

phloem.definition: (botany) tissue that conducts synthesized food substances (e.g., from leaves) to parts where needed; consists primarily of sieve tubes

sieve_tube.definition: tube formed by cells joined end-to-end through which nutrients flow in flowering plants and brown algae

stele (vascular_tissue).definition: the usually cylindrical central vascular portion of the axis of a vascular plant

tracheid.definition: long tubular cell peculiar to xylem

vascular_bundle.definition: a unit strand of the vascular system in stems and leaves of higher plants consisting essentially of xylem and phloem

vein (vascular_bundle).definition: any of the vascular bundles or ribs that form the branching framework of conducting and supporting tissues in a leaf or other plant organ

midrib.definition: the vein in the center of a leaf

vascular_ray.definition: a sheet of vascular tissue separating the vascular bundles

xylem.definition: the woody part of plants: the supporting and water-conducting tissue, consisting primarily of tracheids and vessels

pollen_tube.definition: (botany) a slender tubular outgrowth from a pollen grain when deposited on the stigma for a flower; it penetrates the style and conveys the male gametes to the ovule

prophyll.definition: a plant structure resembling a leaf

receptacle (plant_part).definition: enlarged tip of a stem that bears the floral parts

gynobase.definition: the enlarged receptacle in which the pistil is borne

stipule.definition: a small leafy outgrowth at the base of a leaf or its stalk; usually occurring in pairs and soon shed

stock (plant_part).definition: a plant or stem onto which a graft is made; especially a plant grown specifically to provide the root part of grafted plants

rootstock.definition: root or part of a root used for plant propagation; especially that part of a grafted plant that supplies the roots

stub.definition: a short piece remaining on a trunk or stem where a branch is lost

stump (plant_part).definition: the base part of a tree that remains standing after the tree has been felled

stool (stump).definition: (forestry) the stump of a tree that has been felled or headed for the production of saplings

tendril.definition: slender stem-like structure by which some twining plants attach themselves to an object for support

tepal.definition: an undifferentiated part of a perianth that cannot be distinguished as a sepal or a petal (as in lilies and tulips)

thallus.definition: a plant body without true stems or roots or leaves or vascular system; characteristic of the thallophytes

crustose_thallus.definition: thin crusty lichen thallus; adheres closely to or is embedded in the surface on which it grows

veil.definition: a membranous covering attached to the immature fruiting body of certain mushrooms

partial_veil.definition: membrane of the young sporophore of various mushrooms extending from the margin of the cap to the stem and is ruptured by growth; represented in mature mushroom by an annulus around the stem and sometimes a cortina on the margin of the cap

cortina.definition: a cobwebby partial veil consisting of silky fibrils

universal_veil.definition: membrane initially completely investing the young sporophore of various mushrooms that is ruptured by growth; represented in the mature mushroom by a volva around lower part of stem and scales on upper surface of the cap

volva.definition: cuplike structure around the base of the stalk of certain fungi

radio_source.definition: an object that radiates radio waves

rock (natural_object).definition: a lump or mass of hard consolidated mineral matter

bedrock.definition: solid unweathered rock lying beneath surface deposits of soil

boulder.definition: a large smooth mass of rock detached from its place of origin

glacial_boulder.definition: a boulder that has been carried by a glacier to a place far distant from its place of origin

river_boulder.definition: a boulder that has been carried by a river to a place remote from its place of origin

shore_boulder.definition: a boulder found on a shore remote from its place of origin

calculus.definition: a hard lump produced by the concretion of mineral salts; found in hollow organs or ducts of the body

bladder_stone.definition: a calculus formed in the bladder

enterolith.definition: a calculus occurring in the intestines

gallstone.definition: a calculus formed in the gall bladder or its ducts

kidney_stone.definition: a calculus formed in the kidney

sialolith.definition: a stone formed in the salivary gland

chondrite.definition: a rock of meteoric origin containing chondrules

clastic_rock.definition: (geology) a rock composed of broken pieces of older rocks

crystal (rock).definition: a rock formed by the solidification of a substance; has regularly repeating internal structure; external plane faces

crystallite.definition: any of numerous minute rudimentary crystalline bodies of unknown composition found in glassy igneous rock

intrusion.definition: rock produced by an intrusive process

outcrop.definition: the part of a rock formation that appears above the surface of the surrounding land

belay.definition: something to which a mountain climber's rope can be secured

outthrust.definition: an outcropping of rock that extends outward

petrifaction.definition: a rock created by petrifaction; an organic object infiltrated with mineral matter and preserved in its original form

sill (rock).definition: (geology) a flat (usually horizontal) mass of igneous rock between two layers of older sedimentary rock

stepping_stone.definition: a stone in a marsh or shallow water that can be stepped on in crossing

tor (rock).definition: a prominent rock or pile of rocks on a hill

wall_rock.definition: a rock immediately adjacent to a vein or fault

whinstone.definition: any of various hard colored rocks (especially rocks consisting of chert or basalt)

xenolith.definition: (geology) a piece of rock of different origin from the igneous rock in which it is embedded

sample.definition: all or part of a natural object that is collected and preserved as an example of its class

core (sample).definition: a cylindrical sample of soil or rock obtained with a hollow drill

specimen.definition: a bit of tissue or blood or urine that is taken for diagnostic purposes

cytologic_specimen.definition: a specimen used for cytologic examination and diagnosis

smear.definition: a thin tissue or blood sample spread on a glass slide and stained for cytologic examination and diagnosis under a microscope

alimentary_tract_smear.definition: any of several cytologic smears obtained from different parts of the alimentary tract; obtained by specialized lavage techniques and used mainly to diagnose cancer in those parts

esophageal_smear.definition: alimentary tract smear of material obtained from the esophagus

gastric_smear.definition: alimentary tract smear of material obtained from the stomach

oral_smear.definition: alimentary tract smear of material obtained from the mouth

paraduodenal_smear.definition: alimentary tract smear of material obtained from the duodenum

cervical_smear.definition: a sample of secretions and superficial cells of the uterine cervix and uterus; examined with a microscope to detect any abnormal cells

lower_respiratory_tract_smear.definition: any of several cytologic smears obtained from different parts of the lower respiratory tract; used for cytologic study of cancer and other diseases of the lungs

vaginal_smear.definition: smear taken from the vaginal mucosa for cytological analysis

tangle.definition: a twisted and tangled mass that is highly interwoven

hairball.definition: a compact mass of hair that forms in the alimentary canal (especially in the stomach of animals as a result of licking fur)

shag (tangle).definition: a matted tangle of hair or fiber

closed_universe.definition: (cosmology) a universe that is spatially closed and in which there is sufficient matter to halt the expansion that began with the big bang; the visible matter is only 10 percent of the matter required for closure but there may be large amounts of dark matter

natural_order.definition: the physical universe considered as an orderly system subject to natural (not human or supernatural) laws

nature.definition: the natural physical world including plants and animals and landscapes etc.
